"""trueup plan <library> [--max N]: the model proposes new scenarios as data; code decides.

The planner reads the library's wrapper source from its venv, the scenario
library and the latest findings, and asks the model for new scenarios as JSON.
Every proposal is checked by trueup.scenarios.proposed (schema, app and fake
behaviour exist, truth matches an untraced run). A rejected proposal goes back
to the model with the reason, at most REVISIONS times. Accepted ones are saved
to scenarios/proposed/<library>/ for `trueup sweep <library> --proposed`.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Callable

from trueup import tracing
from trueup.model import PLAN_MODEL, ModelClient, ModelError, record_spend
from trueup.scenarios import ALL
from trueup.scenarios import proposed as prop

REVISIONS = 2
SOURCE_LIMIT = 60_000  # characters of wrapper source sent to the model
FILE_LIMIT = 32_000

# Wrapper files per library, relative to site-packages, most relevant first.
WRAPPER_FILES = {
    "neatlogs": ["neatlogs/openai.py", "neatlogs/anthropic.py"],
    "openllmetry": ["opentelemetry/instrumentation/openai/shared/chat_wrappers.py",
                    "opentelemetry/instrumentation/anthropic/streaming.py",
                    "opentelemetry/instrumentation/openai/v1/responses_wrappers.py"],
    "openinference": ["openinference/instrumentation/openai/_stream.py",
                      "openinference/instrumentation/openai/_request.py",
                      "openinference/instrumentation/anthropic/_stream.py"],
}

SYSTEM = """You plan test scenarios for Trueup, which checks whether an AI tracing library's spans match \
what really happened. A scenario runs one existing app function against a fake provider; the fake model name \
picks the fake's behaviour. You cannot write code: a scenario is JSON data that combines an existing app with an \
existing fake model, plus the truth you expect the run to produce.

Propose scenarios that are NEW (an app + fake model pair not already in the library) and likely to expose a \
tracing bug, given the wrapper source: code paths the existing scenarios miss (a different app reading style on \
the same failure, streaming vs non-streaming, async, tools with errors, refusal through streaming, ...).

Expected truth fields (only listed ones are checked, against what the fake really did):
  calls: number of requests the fake received
  outcome: "ok" or "exception" (what the app saw); exception: the exception class name when outcome is exception
  fake: per call, what the fake did: complete, failed, incomplete, error_event, cut, http_error
  tokens: per call {"input": n, "output": n}, or null when the fake sent no usage
  finish: per call, list of finish reasons / response status
  tool_calls: per call, list of tool names the model asked for
  tool_runs: framework apps only, [{"name", "outcome": "ok"|"raised"}]
  include_usage: per call, whether the app's request asked for stream usage
Facts about the fake: OpenAI replies use 11 input / 7 output tokens, Anthropic 5 / 3. Streams send usage only \
when the app asks (include_usage) on chat; Responses and Anthropic streams always send it. Leave out a field \
when unsure rather than guess; calls, outcome and fake are required, and exception is required when outcome is \
"exception". Each app's "e.g." is what an existing scenario with it does: keep "does" true to the app (an app \
that does not stream does not stream, whatever the fake model).

Reply with JSON only, no prose: {"proposals": [{"id": "p-...", "provider", "api", "framework", "does", "app", \
"model", "expected": {...}, "rationale": "why a wrapper might get this wrong"}]}"""


def wrapper_source(root: Path, library: str) -> str:
    site = next((root / ".trueup" / "venvs" / library / "lib").glob("python*/site-packages"), None)
    if site is None:
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"no venv for {library}; run `trueup sweep {library}` first")
    parts, total = [], 0
    for rel in WRAPPER_FILES[library]:
        f = site / rel
        if not f.exists() or total >= SOURCE_LIMIT:
            continue
        text = f.read_text()[: min(FILE_LIMIT, SOURCE_LIMIT - total)]
        total += len(text)
        parts.append(f"### {rel}\n{text}")
    return "\n\n".join(parts)


def latest_findings(root: Path, library: str) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    runs = sorted((root / ".trueup" / "runs").glob(f"*-{library}/findings.json"))
    if not runs:
        return []
    d = json.loads(runs[-1].read_text())
    out = [{"title": f["title"], "severity": f["severity"], "check": f["details"]["check"],
            "scenarios": f["details"]["scenarios"]} for f in d["findings"]]
    out += [{"title": f.get("title"), "verdict": "disputed"} for f in d.get("disputed_semantics", [])]
    return out


def library_summary() -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    return [{"id": s.id, "app": s.app, "model": s.model, "framework": s.framework} for s in ALL] + [
        {"id": s.id, "app": s.app, "model": s.model, "framework": s.framework, "proposed": True}
        for s in prop.load()]


def first_prompt(library: str, source: str, findings: list[dict[str, Any]], n: int) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
    user = (f"Library under test: {library}.\n\nWhat a scenario may use:\n{json.dumps(prop.catalogue())}\n\n"
            f"Existing scenarios (do not repeat an app + model pair):\n{json.dumps(library_summary())}\n\n"
            f"Current findings for {library}:\n{json.dumps(findings)}\n\n"
            f"Wrapper source of {library} as installed:\n{source}\n\nPropose at most {n} new scenarios.")
    return [{"role": "system", "content": SYSTEM}, {"role": "user", "content": user}]


def revision_prompt(p: Any, reasons: list[str]) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
    user = (f"What a scenario may use:\n{json.dumps(prop.catalogue())}\n\nExisting app + model pairs:\n"
            f"{json.dumps(sorted({f'{s.app}+{s.model}' for s in ALL}))}\n\nYour proposal:\n{json.dumps(p)}\n\n"
            "It was rejected:\n- " + "\n- ".join(reasons) +
            '\n\nFix it and reply with JSON only: {"proposals": [<the one fixed proposal>]}.'
            ' Reply {"proposals": []} to withdraw it.')
    return [{"role": "system", "content": SYSTEM}, {"role": "user", "content": user}]


def check(p: Any, taken: set[tuple[str, str]], ids: set[str],
          untraced: Callable[[dict[str, Any]], tuple[list[str], Any]]) -> list[str]:
    reasons = prop.validate(p, taken, ids)
    if reasons:
        return reasons
    diffs, truth = untraced(p)
    if not diffs and truth and p["api"] == "chat" and "include_usage" not in p["expected"]:
        # The untraced run has no library, so its request shows what the app itself asks for.
        # Without this the comparer guesses from tokens and can report a library change that is not one.
        p["expected"]["include_usage"] = truth["include_usage"]
    return diffs


def plan(root: Path, library: str, max_n: int = 5, *, client: ModelClient | None = None,
         run_id: str | None = None, out: Callable[[str], None] = print,
         untraced: Callable[[dict[str, Any]], tuple[list[str], Any]] = prop.untraced_check,
         save: bool = True) -> dict[str, Any]:
    from trueup.sweep import new_run_id

    run_id = run_id or new_run_id(f"plan-{library}")
    run_dir = root / ".trueup" / "runs" / run_id
    run_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    client = client or ModelClient()
    record_spend(run_dir, "before", client)
    result: dict[str, Any] = {"run_id": run_id, "library": library, "model": PLAN_MODEL, "max": max_n,
                              "session_id": tracing.session_id(), "proposals": [], "accepted": [], "rejected": [],
                              "error": None}
    try:
        with tracing.worker("trueup-planner") as span:
            _plan(root, library, max_n, client, result, out, untraced, save)
            tracing.set_verdict(span, f"accepted {len(result['accepted'])}, rejected {len(result['rejected'])}")
    except ModelError as e:
        result["error"] = str(e)
        out(f"planner stopped: {e}")
    finally:
        record_spend(run_dir, "after", client)
        spend = json.loads((run_dir / "spend.json").read_text())
        result["usage"], result["cost_usd"] = spend.get("usage"), spend.get("run_cost_usd")
        (run_dir / "plan.json").write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=1, default=str))
    out(f"proposals: {len(result['proposals'])}  accepted: {len(result['accepted'])}  "
        f"rejected: {len(result['rejected'])}")
    for r in result["rejected"]:
        out(f"  rejected {r['id']}: {'; '.join(r['reasons'])}")
    out(f"tokens: {client.usage.input_tokens} in, {client.usage.output_tokens} out; "
        f"cost ${result['cost_usd'] if result['cost_usd'] is not None else '?'}; wrote {run_dir}")
    return result


def _plan(root: Path, library: str, max_n: int, client: ModelClient, result: dict[str, Any],
          out: Callable[[str], None], untraced: Callable[..., Any], save: bool) -> None:
    source = wrapper_source(root, library)
    findings = latest_findings(root, library)
    out(f"planning for {library}: {len(source)} chars of wrapper source, {len(findings)} findings")
    reply = client.chat_json(PLAN_MODEL, first_prompt(library, source, findings, max_n))
    props = reply.get("proposals") if isinstance(reply, dict) else None
    if not isinstance(props, list):
        raise ModelError('model reply has no "proposals" list; stopping the planner')
    existing = prop.load()
    taken = {(s.app, s.model) for s in existing}
    ids = {s.id for s in existing}
    for p in props[:max_n]:
        result["proposals"].append(p)
        pid = p.get("id", "?") if isinstance(p, dict) else "?"
        history = []
        for attempt in range(REVISIONS + 1):
            reasons = check(p, taken, ids, untraced)
            if not reasons:
                break
            history.append({"proposal": p, "reasons": reasons})
            out(f"  {pid}: rejected ({'; '.join(reasons)[:200]})")
            if attempt == REVISIONS:
                break
            rev = client.chat_json(PLAN_MODEL, revision_prompt(p, reasons))
            revised = rev.get("proposals") if isinstance(rev, dict) else None
            if not revised:
                history.append({"proposal": None, "reasons": ["withdrawn by the model"]})
                reasons = ["withdrawn by the model after: " + "; ".join(reasons)]
                break
            p = revised[0]
        if reasons:
            result["rejected"].append({"id": pid, "reasons": reasons, "tries": len(history), "history": history})
            continue
        taken.add((p["app"], p["model"]))
        ids.add(p["id"])
        path = prop.save(p, library) if save else None
        result["accepted"].append({"id": p["id"], "revisions": len(history), "proposal": p,
                                   "path": str(path) if path else None})
        out(f"  {p['id']}: accepted{f' after {len(history)} revision(s)' if history else ''}")
"""Per-library venvs under .trueup/venvs/<lib>, built with uv."""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import shutil
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

from trueup.runner.setups import PACKAGES

STAMP = "trueup-packages.json"


class VenvError(RuntimeError):
    pass


def venv_dir(root: Path, library: str) -> Path:
    return root.resolve() / ".trueup" / "venvs" / library


def python_path(root: Path, library: str) -> Path:
    return venv_dir(root, library) / "bin" / "python"


def is_ready(root: Path, library: str) -> bool:
    stamp = venv_dir(root, library) / STAMP
    if not stamp.exists() or not python_path(root, library).exists():
        return False
    try:
        return json.loads(stamp.read_text()) == PACKAGES[library]
    except ValueError:
        return False


def ensure(root: Path, library: str, timeout: float = 900) -> Path:
    """Create the venv if missing or out of date. Returns its python."""
    if library not in PACKAGES:
        raise VenvError(f"unknown library {library!r}")
    py = python_path(root, library)
    if is_ready(root, library):
        return py
    uv = shutil.which("uv")
    if uv is None:
        raise VenvError("uv not found on PATH")
    d = venv_dir(root, library)
    d.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    steps = [
        [uv, "venv", "--quiet", "--allow-existing", "--python", "3.12", str(d)],
        [uv, "pip", "install", "--quiet", "--python", str(py), *PACKAGES[library]],
    ]
    for cmd in steps:
        try:
            p = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout)
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
            raise VenvError(f"timed out: {' '.join(cmd[:3])}") from None
        if p.returncode != 0:
            raise VenvError(f"{' '.join(cmd[:3])} failed: {(p.stderr or p.stdout).strip()[-500:]}")
    (d / STAMP).write_text(json.dumps(PACKAGES[library]))
    return py


def _run(cmd: list[str], timeout: float, cwd: Path | None = None) -> str:
    try:
        p = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout, cwd=cwd)
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
        raise VenvError(f"timed out: {' '.join(cmd[:3])}") from None
    if p.returncode != 0:
        raise VenvError(f"{' '.join(cmd[:3])} failed: {(p.stderr or p.stdout).strip()[-500:]}")
    return p.stdout


def upgrade(root: Path, library: str, timeout: float = 900) -> Path:
    """Bring the library's venv to the latest releases on PyPI. Returns its python."""
    py = ensure(root, library, timeout)
    uv = shutil.which("uv") or "uv"
    _run([uv, "pip", "install", "--quiet", "--upgrade", "--python", str(py), *PACKAGES[library]], timeout)
    return py


# The library's main branch: repo, and local package paths that replace PyPI distributions.
MAIN_SOURCES: dict[str, dict[str, object]] = {
    "neatlogs": {"repo": "https://github.com/neatlogs/neatlogs", "paths": {"neatlogs": "."}},
    "openinference": {
        "repo": "https://github.com/Arize-ai/openinference",
        "paths": {
            "openinference-semantic-conventions": "python/openinference-semantic-conventions",
            "openinference-instrumentation": "python/openinference-instrumentation",
            **{f"openinference-instrumentation-{n}": f"python/instrumentation/openinference-instrumentation-{n}"
               for n in ("openai", "anthropic", "langchain", "openai-agents")},
        },
    },
    "openllmetry": {
        "repo": "https://github.com/traceloop/openllmetry",
        "paths": {
            "opentelemetry-semantic-conventions-ai": "packages/opentelemetry-semantic-conventions-ai",
            **{f"opentelemetry-instrumentation-{n}": f"packages/opentelemetry-instrumentation-{n}"
               for n in ("openai", "anthropic", "langchain", "openai-agents")},
            "traceloop-sdk": "packages/traceloop-sdk",
        },
    },
}


def clone_dir(root: Path, library: str) -> Path:
    return root.resolve() / ".trueup" / "src" / str(MAIN_SOURCES[library]["repo"]).rsplit("/", 1)[1]


def ensure_main(root: Path, library: str, timeout: float = 1200) -> tuple[Path, str]:
    """Shallow-clone main and install its packages into .trueup/venvs/<lib>-main. Returns (python, commit)."""
    src = MAIN_SOURCES[library]
    paths: dict[str, str] = src["paths"]  # type: ignore[assignment]
    clone = clone_dir(root, library)
    git = shutil.which("git") or "git"
    if not (clone / ".git").exists():
        clone.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        _run([git, "clone", "--quiet", "--depth", "1", str(src["repo"]), str(clone)], timeout)
    commit = _run([git, "-C", str(clone), "rev-parse", "HEAD"], 60).strip()
    d = venv_dir(root, f"{library}-main")
    py = d / "bin" / "python"
    stamp = {"commit": commit, "packages": PACKAGES[library]}
    if py.exists() and (d / STAMP).exists() and json.loads((d / STAMP).read_text()) == stamp:
        return py, commit
    uv = shutil.which("uv") or "uv"
    pypi = [p for p in PACKAGES[library] if p not in paths]
    _run([uv, "venv", "--quiet", "--allow-existing", "--python", "3.12", str(d)], timeout)
    _run([uv, "pip", "install", "--quiet", "--python", str(py), *pypi, *(str(clone / p) for p in paths.values())],
         timeout)
    (d / STAMP).write_text(json.dumps(stamp))
    return py, commit
"""Parent side: run one scenario in a fresh subprocess and read its observation."""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import subprocess
import tempfile
import time
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

from trueup.runner.setups import CHILD_ENV, CHILD_ENV_DROP
from trueup.scenarios import BUILT, get

SRC = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]  # .../src
RAN = "ran"
NOT_RUN = "not_run"


def child_env(base: dict[str, str] | None = None) -> dict[str, str]:
    env = dict(os.environ if base is None else base)
    for k in CHILD_ENV_DROP:
        env.pop(k, None)
    env.update(CHILD_ENV)
    env["PYTHONPATH"] = str(SRC)
    env.pop("VIRTUAL_ENV", None)
    return env


def not_run(scenario_id: str, library: str, reason: str, seconds: float = 0.0, detail: str | None = None) -> dict[str, Any]:
    return {"scenario": scenario_id, "library": library, "status": NOT_RUN, "reason": reason,
            "detail": detail, "seconds": round(seconds, 3), "observation": None}


def _last_line(text: str) -> str:
    lines = [ln for ln in text.strip().splitlines() if ln.strip()]
    return lines[-1].strip() if lines else "no output"


def run_scenario(python: Path, library: str, scenario_id: str, timeout: float = 90) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Returns {scenario, library, status, reason, seconds, observation}."""
    try:
        scenario = get(scenario_id)
    except KeyError as e:
        return not_run(scenario_id, library, str(e))
    if scenario.status != BUILT:
        return not_run(scenario_id, library, f"scenario is {scenario.status}")
    return _run_child(python, library, scenario_id, [library, scenario_id], timeout)


def run_audit(python: Path, library: str, script: Path, label: str, overrides: dict[str, str],
              timeout: float = 90) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Run a user's script's main() with the fake answering as `overrides` say. Same shape as run_scenario."""
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="trueup-") as tmp:
        ov = Path(tmp) / "overrides.json"
        ov.write_text(json.dumps(overrides))
        return _run_child(python, library, label, ["--audit", library, str(script.resolve()), str(ov)], timeout)


def _run_child(python: Path, library: str, label: str, args: list[str], timeout: float) -> dict[str, Any]:
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="trueup-") as tmp:
        out = Path(tmp) / "obs.json"
        cmd = [str(python), "-m", "trueup.runner.child", *args, str(out)]
        t0 = time.monotonic()
        try:
            p = subprocess.run(cmd, env=child_env(), cwd=tmp, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout)
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
            return not_run(label, library, f"timed out after {timeout:.0f} s", time.monotonic() - t0)
        except OSError as e:
            return not_run(label, library, f"could not start {python}: {e}")
        seconds = time.monotonic() - t0
        if not out.exists():
            tail = (p.stderr or p.stdout).strip()[-2000:]
            return not_run(label, library, f"child exited {p.returncode} without output: {_last_line(tail)}",
                           seconds, detail=tail)
        payload = json.loads(out.read_text())
    if not payload["ok"]:
        return not_run(label, library, "setup or harness error: " + _last_line(payload["error"]), seconds,
                       detail=payload["error"])
    return {"scenario": label, "library": library, "status": RAN, "reason": None,
            "seconds": round(seconds, 3), "observation": payload["observation"]}
"""trueup sweep <library> [--framework ...]: run the scenarios against one library."""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import time
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Callable

from trueup import tracing
from trueup.core import report
from trueup.core.compare import compare, leads
from trueup.core.model import Mismatch, Observation
from trueup.runner import NOT_RUN, RAN, run_scenario, venvs
from trueup.runner.run import not_run
from trueup.scenarios import FRAMEWORKS, select
from trueup.scenarios.proposed import load as load_proposed


def new_run_id(library: str) -> str:
    return datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ") + f"-{library}"


def summary_line(r: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
    sid = r["scenario"]
    if r["status"] != RAN:
        return f"{sid:30} NOT RUN  {r['reason']}"
    t, tr = r["observation"]["truth"], r["observation"]["trace"]
    app = t["app"]["outcome"] if t["outcome"] == "ok" else f"raised {t['exception']}"
    spans = ", ".join(f"{s['name']}={s['status']['code']}" for s in tr["spans"]) or "none"
    line = f"{sid:30} ran {r['seconds']:5.1f}s  app {app}; fake calls {t['calls']}; spans {len(tr['spans'])}: {spans}"
    if t.get("expected_mismatch"):
        line += f"  [truth differs from scenario expectation: {', '.join(t['expected_mismatch'])}]"
    return line


def sweep(
    root: Path,
    library: str,
    framework: str = "all",
    *,
    proposed: str | None = None,
    ensure: Callable[[Path, str], Path] = venvs.ensure,
    run: Callable[..., dict[str, Any]] = run_scenario,
    out: Callable[[str], None] = print,
) -> tuple[Path, list[dict[str, Any]]]:
    run_id = new_run_id(library) + ("-proposed" if proposed else "")
    run_dir = root / ".trueup" / "runs" / run_id
    run_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    started = time.monotonic()
    scenarios = select(framework) if proposed is None else [
        s for s in load_proposed(proposed) if framework == "all" or s.framework in FRAMEWORKS[framework]]
    try:
        out(f"preparing venv for {library}")
        python: Path | None = ensure(root, library)
        venv_error = None
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 - every scenario is reported NOT RUN
        python, venv_error = None, f"venv not ready: {e}"
    results = []
    with tracing.worker("trueup-runner") as span:
        for s in scenarios:
            r = not_run(s.id, library, venv_error) if python is None else run(python, library, s.id)
            results.append(r)
            out(summary_line(r))
        tracing.set_verdict(span, f"ran {sum(r['status'] == RAN for r in results)}/{len(results)}")
    with tracing.worker("trueup-comparer") as span:
        for r in results:
            if r["status"] == RAN:
                r["mismatches"] = [m.to_dict() for m in compare(Observation.from_dict(r["observation"]))]
            (run_dir / f"{r['scenario']}.json").write_text(json.dumps(r, indent=1, default=str))
        n = sum(len(leads([Mismatch.from_dict(m) for m in r.get("mismatches", [])])) for r in results)
        tracing.set_verdict(span, f"{n} leads")
    ran = sum(r["status"] == RAN for r in results)
    by = by_scenario(results)
    c = report.counts(by)
    table = report.table(by)
    totals = (f"leads: {c['leads']} (high {c['by_severity']['high']}, medium {c['by_severity']['medium']}, "
              f"low {c['by_severity']['low']})  notes: {c['notes']}")
    lines = [
        f"trueup sweep {library} --framework {framework}{f' --proposed {proposed}' if proposed else ''}  run {run_id}",
        f"scenarios: {len(results)}  ran: {ran}  not run: {len(results) - ran}  "
        f"time: {time.monotonic() - started:.0f} s",
        totals,
        "A lead is a disagreement between truth and trace, not a confirmed bug.",
        "",
        *(summary_line(r) for r in results),
        "",
        table,
    ]
    (run_dir / "summary.txt").write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
    (run_dir / "index.json").write_text(json.dumps({
        "run_id": run_id,
        "library": library,
        "framework": framework,
        "proposed": proposed,
        "scenarios": [{"id": r["scenario"], "status": r["status"], "reason": r["reason"]} for r in results],
    }, indent=1))
    not_run_list = [{"scenario": r["scenario"], "reason": r["reason"]} for r in results if r["status"] != RAN]
    (run_dir / "leads.json").write_text(json.dumps(report.leads_payload(run_id, library, by, not_run_list), indent=1,
                                                   default=str))
    out("")
    out(table)
    out(totals)
    out(f"ran {ran}/{len(results)}; wrote {run_dir}")
    return run_dir, results


def by_scenario(results: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> list[tuple[str, list[Mismatch]]]:
    return [(r["scenario"], [Mismatch.from_dict(m) for m in r.get("mismatches", [])])
            for r in results if r["status"] == RAN]


def exit_code(results: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> int:
    """1 if any lead, else 2 if any scenario could not run, else 0."""
    if any(leads([m for _, ms in by_scenario(results) for m in ms])):
        return 1
    return 2 if not results or any(r["status"] == NOT_RUN for r in results) else 0

content.content:
entire search — Search checkpoints, commits, and sessions using semantic and keyword matching
Search checkpoints, commits, and sessions using hybrid search (semantic + keyword),
powered by the Entire search service.

Requires authentication via 'entire login' (GitHub device flow).

By default, results are scoped to the current repository. Use --all-repos to
search across all accessible repos.

Run without arguments to open an interactive search. Results are
displayed in an interactive table. Use --json for machine-readable output,
and add --compact for a trimmed per-result shape suited to agents (implies
--json): id, type, repo, branch, author, date, files touched, score, match
snippet, and a truncated title instead of the full prompt (repo hits add
description and checkpoint count). Fetch full detail
for a single result with 'entire checkpoint explain <id>', or add --full to
that command to pull the checkpoint's entire session transcript. For a
checkpoint hit from another repo, add --repo gh/<owner>/<repo> for a GitHub
mirror or --repo et/<project>/<repo> for an Entire-native repo. The forge
prefix and full checkpoint ID are required; this is unrelated to this
command's --repo filter below.

CLI queries also support inline filters like author:<name>, date:<week|month>,
branch:<name>, repo:<owner/name>, and repo:* to search all accessible repos.

Examples:
entire search "retry backoff" --json
  entire search "retry backoff" --json --compact
  entire search "auth timeout author:alice date:week"
  entire search --code "parseToken"

Current repo: gh/Jennycruzy/trueup  (auto-detected from origin; pass --repo only for a DIFFERENT repo)

Flags:
      --all-repos        Search all accessible repos instead of just the current one
      --author string    Filter by author name
      --branch string    Filter by branch name
      --case-sensitive   Case-sensitive code search (only with --code)
      --code             Search code content across repositories
      --compact          Trimmed JSON output for agents: id, repo, files touched, score, match snippet, and a truncated title instead of the full prompt (implies --json)
      --date string      Filter by time period (week or month)
      --json             Output as JSON
      --limit int        Maximum number of results (per page for checkpoint search, total for --code) (default 10)
      --page int         Page number (1-based) (default 1)
      --repo strings     Filter by repository (gh/owner/repo, et/proj/repo, owner/repo, ULID, or *); repeatable and comma-separated for multiple repos

content.content:
entire plugin — Manage Entire plugins (install, list, upgrade, search, remove)
Manage Entire plugins.

Plugins are external executables named 'entire-<name>'. The CLI discovers
plugins on $PATH and from a per-user managed directory which is
auto-prepended to PATH at startup. The managed directory is, in order of
precedence:

  $ENTIRE_PLUGIN_DIR/bin (override)
  $XDG_DATA_HOME/entire/plugins/bin (Linux/macOS, when set)
  ~/.local/share/entire/plugins/bin (Linux/macOS default)
  %LOCALAPPDATA%\entire\plugins\bin (Windows, when set)
  ~\AppData\Local\entire\plugins\bin (Windows fallback when LOCALAPPDATA is unset)

Install sources:
  entire plugin install run                                    index lookup
  entire plugin install https://github.com/entireio/entire-run repository URL
  entire plugin install ./dist/entire-run                      local executable

Remote installs resolve the newest semver tag over the git protocol, then
download the platform's release asset (verified against the release's
checksums.txt when published). Discovery uses a git-synced plugin index;
see 'entire plugin search' and 'entire plugin index update'.

"""OpenTelemetry OpenAI Agents instrumentation"""

import os
from typing import Collection
from opentelemetry.trace import get_tracer
from opentelemetry.metrics import Meter, get_meter
from opentelemetry.instrumentation.instrumentor import BaseInstrumentor
from opentelemetry.instrumentation.openai_agents.version import __version__
from opentelemetry.semconv_ai import Meters


_instruments = ("openai-agents >= 0.2.0",)


class OpenAIAgentsInstrumentor(BaseInstrumentor):
    """An instrumentor for OpenAI Agents SDK."""

    def __init__(self, *, replace_existing_processors: bool = False) -> None:
        """Initialize the instrumentor.

        Args:
            replace_existing_processors:
                If enabled, any existing trace processors
                will be cleared before this processor is added as the only one.
                By default, the openai-agents library has
                a built-in tracing processor that is always active,
                and this processor will be added alongside it,
                resulting in traces being sent to multiple backends.
        """
        super().__init__()
        self._replace_existing_processors: bool = replace_existing_processors

    def instrumentation_dependencies(self) -> Collection[str]:
        return _instruments

    def _instrument(self, **kwargs) -> None:
        """Override the abstract base method and instrument openai-agents.

        Args:
            tracer_provider: An optional TracerProvider to use
                when creating a Tracer.
            meter_provider: An optional MeterProvider to use
                when creating a Meter.

            Additional kwargs are ignored.
        """
        tracer_provider = kwargs.get("tracer_provider")
        tracer = get_tracer(__name__, __version__, tracer_provider)

        meter_provider = kwargs.get("meter_provider")
        meter = get_meter(__name__, __version__, meter_provider)

        if is_metrics_enabled():
            _create_metrics(meter)

        # Use hook-based approach with OpenAI Agents SDK callbacks
        try:
            from agents import add_trace_processor, set_trace_processors
            from ._hooks import OpenTelemetryTracingProcessor

            # Create and add our OpenTelemetry processor
            otel_processor = OpenTelemetryTracingProcessor(tracer)
            if self._replace_existing_processors:
                set_trace_processors([otel_processor])
            else:
                add_trace_processor(otel_processor)

        except Exception:
            # Silently handle import errors - OpenAI Agents SDK may not be available
            pass

        try:
            from ._realtime_wrappers import wrap_realtime_session

            wrap_realtime_session(tracer)
        except Exception:
            pass

    def _uninstrument(self, **kwargs):
        try:
            from ._realtime_wrappers import unwrap_realtime_session

            unwrap_realtime_session()
        except Exception:
            pass


def is_metrics_enabled() -> bool:
    return (os.getenv("TRACELOOP_METRICS_ENABLED") or "true").lower() == "true"


def _create_metrics(meter: Meter):
    token_histogram = meter.create_histogram(
        name=Meters.LLM_TOKEN_USAGE,
        unit="token",
        description="Measures number of input and output tokens used",
    )

    duration_histogram = meter.create_histogram(
        name=Meters.LLM_OPERATION_DURATION,
        unit="s",
        description="GenAI operation duration",
    )

    return token_histogram, duration_histogram

"""Generate a minimal repro script for one scenario under one library. Pure: returns text.

The script runs offline: trueup's local fake provider answers, the API keys are
fake placeholders and export is off. It sets up the library the recommended way,
runs the scenario's app, compares truth with the spans and prints each lead as a
JSON line. It needs trueup's src on PYTHONPATH (for the fake and the app code)
and a venv with the library installed.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

TEMPLATE = '''"""Repro: {library} on scenario {scenario}. {does}
Offline: a local fake provider answers; no API keys, no network.
Run with {library} installed: PYTHONPATH=<trueup>/src python {filename}
"""
import gc, json, os
from trueup.runner.setups import CHILD_ENV, SETUPS, quiet_agents_sdk
os.environ.update(CHILD_ENV)  # content capture on, export off, fake keys
from trueup.core.compare import compare, leads
from trueup.core.model import Observation
from trueup.fake import FakeProvider
from trueup.runner import framework_apps, truth
from trueup.runner.apps import APPS
from trueup.runner.child import span_to_dict
from trueup.scenarios import get

s = get("{scenario}")
exporter, flush = SETUPS["{library}"](s.framework)  # the library's recommended setup
if s.framework == "openai-agents":
    quiet_agents_sdk()  # drop the Agents SDK's own upload to api.openai.com
with FakeProvider() as fake:
    try:
        app = {{"outcome": "ok", "result": APPS[s.app](fake.base_url, s.model)}}
    except Exception as e:
        app = {{"outcome": "exception", "exception_type": type(e).__name__, "message": str(e)}}
    gc.collect()
    flush()
    log = fake.log.entries()
t = {{**truth.derive(log, app, framework_apps.TOOL_RUNS), "expected": s.expected, "app": app, "fake_log": log}}
spans = [span_to_dict(x) for x in exporter.get_finished_spans()]
for m in leads(compare(Observation(t, {{"library": "{library}", "spans": spans}}))):
    print(json.dumps(m.to_dict(), default=str))
'''


def generate(library: str, scenario: str, does: str) -> str:
    return TEMPLATE.format(library=library, scenario=scenario, does=does.strip(),
                           filename=f"{library}-{scenario}.py")


def line_count(text: str) -> int:
    return len(text.rstrip("\n").splitlines())

    "openllmetry": "https://github.com/traceloop/openllmetry",

class Package:
    path: str  # in the repo
    dist: str  # distribution name, as installed in the scenario venv
    tests: str = "tests"  # relative to path
    # Test requirements: "group:<name>" reads [dependency-groups] of the package's pyproject,
    # "file:<name>" a requirements file in the package; anything else is a requirement.
    test_deps: tuple[str, ...] = ()
    # Local packages of the same repo the tests need from source (editable).
    local_deps: tuple[str, ...] = ()


@dataclass(frozen=True)

    library: str
    code_path: str
    packages: tuple[Package, ...]
    seeds: tuple[str, ...]  # wrapper functions or classes to locate
    reference_seeds: tuple[str, ...] = ()  # where the library gets a similar case right
    reference_note: str = ""  # the rule the fix must follow (OTel GenAI conventions)
    extra: dict[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict)


_OLL_SEMCONV = "packages/opentelemetry-semantic-conventions-ai"
_OLL_TEST = ("group:test", "group:dev")
_OI_CORE = ("python/openinference-semantic-conventions", "python/openinference-instrumentation")

"""The model drafts the smallest change plus a unit test; code checks and applies it to the clone.

The draft is JSON: exact search/replace edits on files of the target's packages,
and one new test file in the package's tests directory. Code refuses edits outside
those packages, an `old` text that is not found exactly once, and a test file
outside the tests directory. Whether the patch is kept is decided by verify.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

from trueup.fixer.targets import Target

SYSTEM = """You fix bugs in AI tracing libraries (OpenTelemetry instrumentations). Trueup ran a real agent \
against a fake provider, so it knows what really happened, and found that the library's spans disagree with it. \
You get the finding, the located wrapper code and its callers, and how the right behaviour looks.

Draft the SMALLEST change that makes the spans match what happened, in the library's own style, plus ONE new \
unit test written like the package's existing tests (same fixtures, same imports, no network, no API keys, no \
cassettes) that fails on the current code and passes with your change. Do not change existing tests. Do not \
reformat code you do not change.

Reply with JSON only:
{"explanation": "cause and fix in 2-4 plain sentences",
 "edits": [{"file": "<path from the repo root>", "old": "<exact text in the file, unique, with enough context>", \
"new": "<replacement>"}],
 "test": {"file": "<path from the repo root, in the package's tests dir, new file named test_trueup_*.py>", \
"content": "<the whole test file>"}}"""


class PatchError(ValueError):
    """The draft cannot be applied. The reason goes back to the model."""


def test_style(clone: Path, target: Target, limit: int = 14_000) -> str:
    """conftest.py and the shortest test files of the first package, to show its test style."""
    tests = clone / target.packages[0].path / target.packages[0].tests
    parts, total = [], 0
    files = [tests / "conftest.py"] + sorted((f for f in tests.glob("test_*.py")), key=lambda f: f.stat().st_size)
    for f in files:
        if not f.exists():
            continue
        text = f.read_text(errors="replace")[:8000]
        if total + len(text) > limit:
            break
        total += len(text)
        parts.append(f"### {f.relative_to(clone)}\n{text}")
    return "\n\n".join(parts)


def first_prompt(finding: dict[str, Any], target: Target, located: dict[str, Any], source: str,
                 style: str) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
    d = finding["details"]
    leads = [{k: x.get(k) for k in ("scenario", "field", "truth", "trace")} for x in d.get("leads", [])]
    user = (f"Library: {target.library} (repo commit {located['commit'][:10]}).\n"
            f"Finding {finding['id']}: {finding['title']} (severity {finding['severity']}).\n"
            f"Check: {d['check']}; field: {d['field']}.\nTruth vs trace per scenario:\n{json.dumps(leads)}\n"
            f"Scenarios: {', '.join(d['scenarios'])}. Scenarios of this code path that are right today must stay "
            f"right.\nRight behaviour: {target.reference_note}\nChecker's reference rule: "
            f"{d.get('rules', {}).get('reference', '')}\n\n"
            f"Packages you may change: {', '.join(p.path for p in target.packages)}.\n"
            f"Located definitions:\n{json.dumps(located['definitions'])}\n"
            f"Callers:\n{json.dumps(located['callers'][:60])}\n\n"
            f"Source:\n{source}\n\nTest style of {target.packages[0].path}:\n{style}")
    return [{"role": "system", "content": SYSTEM}, {"role": "user", "content": user}]


def revision_prompt(messages: list[dict[str, str]], draft: Any, reason: str) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
    return [*messages, {"role": "assistant", "content": json.dumps(draft)},
            {"role": "user", "content": "That patch was rejected:\n" + reason +
             "\n\nRevise it. Reply with the whole JSON again (edits against the ORIGINAL files, the full test "
             "file)."}]


def check_draft(draft: Any, clone: Path, target: Target) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
    """The edits plus the test as file writes. Raises PatchError with the reason."""
    if not isinstance(draft, dict) or not isinstance(draft.get("edits"), list) or not draft["edits"]:
        raise PatchError('the reply needs a non-empty "edits" list')

"""trueup fix <finding-id>: locate the wrapper, let the model draft a patch and a test, and verify it.

Steps, one library at a time:
  1. locate (trueup.fixer.locate): shallow clone in .trueup/clones/<lib>; Entire's code graph if it
     is there, else ripgrep + ast; locate.json in the run dir and in fixes/<id>/
  2. baseline (verifier): the target packages' own test suites on the clean clone, and the full
     scenario library in .trueup/venvs/<lib>-fix built from the clean clone
  3. up to MAX_TRIES tries: the model drafts edits + a test (trueup.fixer.patch); code applies them;
     the verifier checks that the new test fails before and passes after, the suites show no new
     failure, the finding's scenarios now match truth, and the full library shows no new mismatch.
     A failed try goes back to the model with the reason.
Writes fixes/<id>/: patch.diff, the test file, before-after.md/json, suites.json, locate.json,
tries.json and summary.md. Nothing is committed, pushed or posted. The clone is reset at the end.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import time
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Callable

from trueup import tracing
from trueup.fixer import locate as loc
from trueup.fixer import patch as pt
from trueup.fixer import targets as tg
from trueup.fixer import verify as vf
from trueup.model import PLAN_MODEL, ModelClient, ModelError, record_spend

MAX_TRIES = 3


def find_finding(root: Path, finding_id: str) -> tuple[dict[str, Any], Path]:
    """The finding with this id in the newest findings.json that has it."""
    for f in sorted((root / ".trueup" / "runs").glob("*/findings.json"), reverse=True):
        for x in json.loads(f.read_text())["findings"]:
            if x["id"] == finding_id:
                return x, f.parent
    raise FileNotFoundError(f"no finding {finding_id!r} in .trueup/runs/*/findings.json")


def all_scenarios() -> list[str]:
    from trueup.scenarios import select
    from trueup.scenarios.proposed import load

    return [s.id for s in select("all")] + [s.id for s in load()]


def _touched(target: tg.Target, files: list[str]) -> list[tg.Package]:
    return [p for p in target.packages if any(f.startswith(p.path.strip("./") + "/" if p.path != "." else "")
                                              for f in files)]


def _short(s: str, n: int = 600) -> str:
    return s if len(s) <= n else s[: n - 3] + "..."


def baseline(root: Path, clone: Path, commit: str, target: tg.Target, fix_dir: Path,
             out: Callable[[str], None]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Suites and sweep on the clean clone. Cached in fix_dir per commit."""
    cache = fix_dir / "baseline.json"
    if cache.exists():
        b = json.loads(cache.read_text())
        if b.get("commit") == commit:
            out("baseline: cached for this commit")
            return b
    out("baseline: building the test venv")
    tpy = vf.ensure_test_venv(root, clone, target)
    suites = {}
    for p in target.packages:
        out(f"baseline: {p.path} test suite (clean clone)")
        suites[p.path] = vf.run_pytest(tpy, clone, p, [p.tests])
        s = suites[p.path]
        out(f"  {s.get('passed', '?')} passed, {s.get('failed', '?')} failed, {s.get('errors', '?')} errors, "
            f"exit {s['exit']}")
    out("baseline: building the scenario venv from the clean clone")
    fpy = vf.ensure_fix_venv(root, clone, target.library)
    vf.reinstall(fpy, clone, target)
    out("baseline: full scenario library")
    sweep = vf.sweep_scenarios(fpy, target.library, all_scenarios(), out=out)
    b = {"commit": commit, "suites": suites, "sweep": sweep}
    cache.write_text(json.dumps(b, indent=1, default=str))
    return b


def verify_try(root: Path, clone: Path, target: tg.Target, finding: dict[str, Any], draft: dict[str, Any],
               writes: list[dict[str, str]], base: dict[str, Any], out: Callable[[str], None]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Apply the try to the clean clone step by step. Returns the try's record with ok and reason."""
    rec: dict[str, Any] = {"ok": False}
    test = draft["test"]
    pkg_of_test = next(p for p in target.packages if test["file"].startswith(
        (p.path.strip("./") + "/" if p.path != "." else "") + p.tests + "/"))
    test_rel = str(Path(test["file"]).relative_to(pkg_of_test.path)) if pkg_of_test.path != "." else test["file"]
    tpy = vf.ensure_test_venv(root, clone, target)
    loc.reset_clone(clone)
    pt.write_files(clone, [{"file": test["file"], "content": test["content"]}])
    out("  new test on the unpatched code")
    t_before = vf.run_pytest(tpy, clone, pkg_of_test, [test_rel])
    pt.write_files(clone, writes)
    out("  new test on the patched code")
    t_after = vf.run_pytest(tpy, clone, pkg_of_test, [test_rel])
    ok, why = vf.new_test_verdict(t_before, t_after)
    rec["new_test"] = {"before": t_before, "after": t_after, "ok": ok, "reason": why}
    out(f"  {why[:300]}")
    if not ok:
        rec["reason"] = why
        return rec
    rec["suites"] = {}
    for p in _touched(target, [w["file"] for w in writes] + [test["file"]]):
        out(f"  {p.path} test suite (patched)")
        after = vf.run_pytest(tpy, clone, p, [p.tests])
        ok, why = vf.suite_verdict(base["suites"][p.path], after, test["file"])
        rec["suites"][p.path] = {"after": after, "ok": ok, "reason": why}
        out(f"  {why[:300]}")
        if not ok:
            rec["reason"] = f"{p.path}: {why}"
            return rec
    fpy = vf.ensure_fix_venv(root, clone, target.library) if False else \
        vf.venvs.venv_dir(root, f"{target.library}-fix") / "bin" / "python"
    vf.reinstall(fpy, clone, target)
    out("  the finding's scenarios (patched)")
    scen = vf.sweep_scenarios(fpy, target.library, finding["details"]["scenarios"], out=out)
    ok, why = vf.scenario_verdict(scen, finding)
    rec["scenarios"] = {"ok": ok, "reason": why}
    out(f"  {why}")
    if not ok:
        rec["reason"] = why
        return rec
    out("  full scenario library (patched)")
    full = vf.sweep_scenarios(fpy, target.library, all_scenarios(), out=out)
    new = vf.new_mismatches(base["sweep"], full)
    rec["sweep"] = {"totals": vf.totals(full), "new_mismatches": new}
    rec["sweep_after"] = full
    if new:
        rec["reason"] = (f"{len(new)} new mismatch(es) in the full scenario library: " +
                         "; ".join(f"{m['scenario']} {m['check']} {m['field']}: truth {m['truth']}, trace "
                                   f"{m['trace']}" for m in new[:8]))
        out(f"  {rec['reason'][:300]}")
        return rec
    ok, why = vf.scenario_verdict(full, finding)
    rec.update(ok=ok, reason=why if ok else f"full sweep: {why}")
    return rec


def fix(root: Path, finding_id: str, *, client: ModelClient | None = None, run_id: str | None = None,
        out: Callable[[str], None] = print, max_tries: int = MAX_TRIES) -> dict[str, Any]:
    from trueup.sweep import new_run_id

    finding, found_in = find_finding(root, finding_id)
    target = tg.get(finding["library"], finding["details"]["code_path"])
    run_id = run_id or new_run_id(f"fix-{finding['library']}")
    run_dir = root / ".trueup" / "runs" / run_id
    fix_dir = root / "fixes" / finding_id
    run_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    fix_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    client = client or ModelClient()
    record_spend(run_dir, "before", client)
    result: dict[str, Any] = {"finding": finding_id, "title": finding["title"], "library": target.library,
                              "found_in": found_in.name, "run_id": run_id, "session_id": tracing.session_id(),
                              "model": PLAN_MODEL, "started": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", time.gmtime()),
                              "tries": [], "fixed": False, "error": None}
    clone = None
    try:
        with tracing.worker("trueup-fixer", step="locate") as span:
            located = loc.locate(root, target, run_dir)
            clone = Path(located["clone"])
            loc.reset_clone(clone)
            (fix_dir / "locate.json").write_text((run_dir / "locate.json").read_text())
            result["commit"], result["locate_method"] = located["commit"], located["method"]
            out(f"located with {located['method']}: {len(located['definitions'])} definitions, "
                f"{len(located['callers'])} callers ({located['graph'].get('reason', '')[:160]})")
            tracing.set_verdict(span, located["method"])
        with tracing.worker("trueup-verifier", step="baseline") as span:
            base = baseline(root, clone, located["commit"], target, fix_dir, out)
            tracing.set_verdict(span, f"baseline: {vf.totals(base['sweep'])['leads']} leads")
        result["suites_before"] = {k: {x: v.get(x) for x in ("total", "passed", "failed", "errors", "skipped",
                                                              "failing", "exit")} for k, v in base["suites"].items()}
        messages = pt.first_prompt(finding, target, located, loc.source_excerpts(clone, located),
                                   pt.test_style(clone, target))
        for n in range(1, max_tries + 1):
            out(f"try {n}/{max_tries}: asking {PLAN_MODEL} for a patch")
            rec: dict[str, Any] = {"try": n}
            with tracing.worker("trueup-fixer", step=f"draft {n}") as span:
                draft = client.chat_json(PLAN_MODEL, messages, max_tokens=12000)
                rec["explanation"] = draft.get("explanation") if isinstance(draft, dict) else None
                rec["draft"] = draft
                try:
                    writes = pt.check_draft(draft, clone, target)
                    tracing.set_verdict(span, "applies")
                except pt.PatchError as e:
                    rec.update(ok=False, stage="apply", reason=f"patch does not apply: {e}")
                    tracing.set_verdict(span, "does not apply")
            if "stage" not in rec:
                with tracing.worker("trueup-verifier", step=f"try {n}") as span:
                    rec.update(verify_try(root, clone, target, finding, draft, writes, base, out))
                    rec["stage"] = "verified" if rec["ok"] else "verify"
                    rec["diff"] = pt.diff(clone)
                    tracing.set_verdict(span, "pass" if rec["ok"] else "fail")
            out(f"try {n}: {'PASS' if rec['ok'] else 'FAIL'}: {_short(rec['reason'], 400)}")
            result["tries"].append(rec)
            if rec["ok"]:
                result["fixed"] = True
                write_fix(fix_dir, finding, target, base, rec)
                break
            messages = pt.revision_prompt(messages, draft, rec["reason"])
    except (ModelError, vf.VerifyError, RuntimeError) as e:
        result["error"] = f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"
        out(f"fixer stopped: {result['error']}")
    finally:
        if clone is not None:
            loc.reset_clone(clone)
        record_spend(run_dir, "after", client)
        spend = json.loads((run_dir / "spend.json").read_text())
        result["usage"], result["cost_usd"] = spend.get("usage"), spend.get("run_cost_usd")
        result["spend_after_usd"] = spend.get("after", {}).get("spend_usd")
        write_log(fix_dir, run_dir, result)
    out(f"{finding_id}: {'fixed, verified' if result['fixed'] else 'NOT fixed'} after {len(result['tries'])} "
        f"tr{'y' if len(result['tries']) == 1 else 'ies'}; model cost ${result['cost_usd']}; wrote {fix_dir}")
    return result


def write_fix(fix_dir: Path, finding: dict[str, Any], target: tg.Target, base: dict[str, Any],
              rec: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
    (fix_dir / "patch.diff").write_text(rec["diff"])
    test = rec["draft"]["test"]
    (fix_dir / Path(test["file"]).name).write_text(test["content"])
    rows = vf.before_after(finding, base["sweep"], rec["sweep_after"])
    tb, ta = vf.totals(base["sweep"]), vf.totals(rec["sweep_after"])
    (fix_dir / "before-after.json").write_text(json.dumps({"rows": rows, "before": tb, "after": ta}, indent=1,
                                                          default=str))
    (fix_dir / "before-after.md").write_text(vf.table_md(rows, tb, ta))


def write_log(fix_dir: Path, run_dir: Path, result: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
    tries = []
    for t in result["tries"]:
        t = {k: v for k, v in t.items() if k != "sweep_after"}
        tries.append(t)
    log = {**result, "tries": tries}
    (fix_dir / "tries.json").write_text(json.dumps(log, indent=1, default=str))
    (run_dir / "fix.json").write_text(json.dumps(log, indent=1, default=str))
    suites = {"before": result.get("suites_before", {}),
              "after": {n: {p: {x: s["after"].get(x) for x in ("total", "passed", "failed", "errors", "skipped",
                                                                  "failing", "exit")} | {"verdict": s["reason"]}
                            for p, s in t.get("suites", {}).items()} for n, t in
                        ((t["try"], t) for t in result["tries"])}}
    (fix_dir / "suites.json").write_text(json.dumps(suites, indent=1, default=str))
    lines = [f"# {result['finding']}", "", result["title"], "",
             f"Library commit: {result.get('commit', '?')}. Located with {result.get('locate_method', '?')}.",
             f"Model: {result['model']}; cost ${result['cost_usd']} (key spend delta); run {result['run_id']}.", "",
             "Result: " + ("fixed: the new test fails before and passes after, the suites show no new failure, the "
                           "finding's scenarios match truth and the full scenario library has no new mismatch."
                           if result["fixed"] else "NOT fixed. No patch is offered."
                           + (f" Stopped: {result['error']}" if result["error"] else "")), "", "## Tries", ""]
    for t in result["tries"]:
        lines.append(f"{t['try']}. {'PASS' if t['ok'] else 'FAIL'} at {t.get('stage')}: {_short(t['reason'], 700)}")
        if t.get("explanation"):
            lines.append(f"   Model's explanation: {_short(t['explanation'], 500)}")
    if (fix_dir / "before-after.md").exists() and result["fixed"]:
        lines += ["", "## Before and after", "", (fix_dir / "before-after.md").read_text()]
    (fix_dir / "summary.md").write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n")

"""trueup fix <finding-id>: locate the wrapper, let the model draft a patch and a test, and verify it.

Steps, one library at a time:
  1. locate (trueup.fixer.locate): shallow clone in .trueup/clones/<lib>; Entire's code graph if it
     is there, else ripgrep + ast; locate.json in the run dir and in fixes/<id>/
  2. baseline (verifier): the target packages' own test suites on the clean clone, and the full
     scenario library in .trueup/venvs/<lib>-fix built from the clean clone
  3. up to MAX_TRIES tries: the model drafts edits + a test (trueup.fixer.patch); code applies them;
     the verifier checks that the new test fails before and passes after, the suites show no new
     failure, the finding's scenarios now match truth, and the full library shows no new mismatch.
     A failed try goes back to the model with the reason.
Writes fixes/<id>/: patch.diff, the test file, before-after.md/json, suites.json, locate.json,
tries.json and summary.md. Nothing is committed, pushed or posted. The clone is reset at the end.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import time
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Callable

from trueup import tracing
from trueup.fixer import locate as loc
from trueup.fixer import patch as pt
from trueup.fixer import targets as tg
from trueup.fixer import verify as vf
from trueup.model import PLAN_MODEL, ModelClient, ModelError, record_spend

MAX_TRIES = 3


def find_finding(root: Path, finding_id: str) -> tuple[dict[str, Any], Path]:
    """The finding with this id in the newest findings.json that has it."""
    for f in sorted((root / ".trueup" / "runs").glob("*/findings.json"), reverse=True):
        for x in json.loads(f.read_text())["findings"]:
            if x["id"] == finding_id:
                return x, f.parent
    raise FileNotFoundError(f"no finding {finding_id!r} in .trueup/runs/*/findings.json")


def all_scenarios() -> list[str]:
    from trueup.scenarios import select
    from trueup.scenarios.proposed import load

    return [s.id for s in select("all")] + [s.id for s in load()]


def _touched(target: tg.Target, files: list[str]) -> list[tg.Package]:
    return [p for p in target.packages if any(f.startswith(p.path.strip("./") + "/" if p.path != "." else "")
                                              for f in files)]


def _short(s: str, n: int = 600) -> str:
    return s if len(s) <= n else s[: n - 3] + "..."


def baseline(root: Path, clone: Path, commit: str, target: tg.Target, fix_dir: Path,
             out: Callable[[str], None]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Suites and sweep on the clean clone. Cached in fix_dir per commit."""
    cache = fix_dir / "baseline.json"
    if cache.exists():
        b = json.loads(cache.read_text())
        if b.get("commit") == commit:
            out("baseline: cached for this commit")
            return b
    out("baseline: building the test venv")
    tpy = vf.ensure_test_venv(root, clone, target)
    suites = {}
    for p in target.packages:
        out(f"baseline: {p.path} test suite (clean clone)")
        suites[p.path] = vf.run_pytest(tpy, clone, p, [p.tests])
        s = suites[p.path]
        out(f"  {s.get('passed', '?')} passed, {s.get('failed', '?')} failed, {s.get('errors', '?')} errors, "
            f"exit {s['exit']}")
    out("baseline: building the scenario venv from the clean clone")
    fpy = vf.ensure_fix_venv(root, clone, target.library)
    vf.reinstall(fpy, clone, target)
    out("baseline: full scenario library")
    sweep = vf.sweep_scenarios(fpy, target.library, all_scenarios(), out=out)
    b = {"commit": commit, "suites": suites, "sweep": sweep}
    cache.write_text(json.dumps(b, indent=1, default=str))
    return b


def verify_try(root: Path, clone: Path, target: tg.Target, finding: dict[str, Any], draft: dict[str, Any],
               writes: list[dict[str, str]], base: dict[str, Any], out: Callable[[str], None]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Apply the try to the clean clone step by step. Returns the try's record with ok and reason."""
    rec: dict[str, Any] = {"ok": False}
    test = draft["test"]
    pkg_of_test = next(p for p in target.packages if test["file"].startswith(
        (p.path.strip("./") + "/" if p.path != "." else "") + p.tests + "/"))
    test_rel = str(Path(test["file"]).relative_to(pkg_of_test.path)) if pkg_of_test.path != "." else test["file"]
    tpy = vf.ensure_test_venv(root, clone, target)
    loc.reset_clone(clone)
    pt.write_files(clone, [{"file": test["file"], "content": test["content"]}])
    out("  new test on the unpatched code")
    t_before = vf.run_pytest(tpy, clone, pkg_of_test, [test_rel])
    pt.write_files(clone, writes)
    out("  new test on the patched code")
    t_after = vf.run_pytest(tpy, clone, pkg_of_test, [test_rel])
    ok, why = vf.new_test_verdict(t_before, t_after)
    rec["new_test"] = {"before": t_before, "after": t_after, "ok": ok, "reason": why}
    out(f"  {why[:300]}")
    if not ok:
        rec["reason"] = why
        return rec
    rec["suites"] = {}
    for p in _touched(target, [w["file"] for w in writes] + [test["file"]]):
        out(f"  {p.path} test suite (patched)")
        after = vf.run_pytest(tpy, clone, p, [p.tests])
        ok, why = vf.suite_verdict(base["suites"][p.path], after, test["file"])
        rec["suites"][p.path] = {"after": after, "ok": ok, "reason": why}
        out(f"  {why[:300]}")
        if not ok:
            rec["reason"] = f"{p.path}: {why}"
            return rec
    fpy = vf.ensure_fix_venv(root, clone, target.library) if False else \
        vf.venvs.venv_dir(root, f"{target.library}-fix") / "bin" / "python"
    vf.reinstall(fpy, clone, target)
    out("  the finding's scenarios (patched)")
    scen = vf.sweep_scenarios(fpy, target.library, finding["details"]["scenarios"], out=out)
    ok, why = vf.scenario_verdict(scen, finding)
    rec["scenarios"] = {"ok": ok, "reason": why}
    out(f"  {why}")
    if not ok:
        rec["reason"] = why
        return rec
    out("  full scenario library (patched)")
    full = vf.sweep_scenarios(fpy, target.library, all_scenarios(), out=out)
    new = vf.new_mismatches(base["sweep"], full)
    rec["sweep"] = {"totals": vf.totals(full), "new_mismatches": new}
    rec["sweep_after"] = full
    if new:
        rec["reason"] = (f"{len(new)} new mismatch(es) in the full scenario library: " +
                         "; ".join(f"{m['scenario']} {m['check']} {m['field']}: truth {m['truth']}, trace "
                                   f"{m['trace']}" for m in new[:8]))
        out(f"  {rec['reason'][:300]}")
        return rec
    ok, why = vf.scenario_verdict(full, finding)
    rec.update(ok=ok, reason=why if ok else f"full sweep: {why}")
    return rec


def fix(root: Path, finding_id: str, *, client: ModelClient | None = None, run_id: str | None = None,
        out: Callable[[str], None] = print, max_tries: int = MAX_TRIES) -> dict[str, Any]:
    from trueup.sweep import new_run_id

    finding, found_in = find_finding(root, finding_id)
    target = tg.get(finding["library"], finding["details"]["code_path"])
    run_id = run_id or new_run_id(f"fix-{finding['library']}")
    run_dir = root / ".trueup" / "runs" / run_id
    fix_dir = root / "fixes" / finding_id
    run_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    fix_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    client = client or ModelClient()
    record_spend(run_dir, "before", client)
    result: dict[str, Any] = {"finding": finding_id, "title": finding["title"], "library": target.library,
                              "found_in": found_in.name, "run_id": run_id, "session_id": tracing.session_id(),
                              "model": PLAN_MODEL, "started": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", time.gmtime()),
                              "tries": [], "fixed": False, "error": None}
    clone = None
    try:
        with tracing.worker("trueup-fixer", step="locate") as span:
            located = loc.locate(root, target, run_dir)
            clone = Path(located["clone"])
            loc.reset_clone(clone)
            (fix_dir / "locate.json").write_text((run_dir / "locate.json").read_text())
            result["commit"], result["locate_method"] = located["commit"], located["method"]
            out(f"located with {located['method']}: {len(located['definitions'])} definitions, "
                f"{len(located['callers'])} callers ({located['graph'].get('reason', '')[:160]})")
            tracing.set_verdict(span, located["method"])
        with tracing.worker("trueup-verifier", step="baseline") as span:
            base = baseline(root, clone, located["commit"], target, fix_dir, out)
            tracing.set_verdict(span, f"baseline: {vf.totals(base['sweep'])['leads']} leads")
        result["suites_before"] = {k: {x: v.get(x) for x in ("total", "passed", "failed", "errors", "skipped",
                                                              "failing", "exit")} for k, v in base["suites"].items()}
        messages = pt.first_prompt(finding, target, located, loc.source_excerpts(clone, located),
                                   pt.test_style(clone, target))
        for n in range(1, max_tries + 1):
            out(f"try {n}/{max_tries}: asking {PLAN_MODEL} for a patch")
            rec: dict[str, Any] = {"try": n}
            with tracing.worker("trueup-fixer", step=f"draft {n}") as span:
                draft = client.chat_json(PLAN_MODEL, messages, max_tokens=12000)
                rec["explanation"] = draft.get("explanation") if isinstance(draft, dict) else None
                rec["draft"] = draft
                try:
                    writes = pt.check_draft(draft, clone, target)
                    tracing.set_verdict(span, "applies")
                except pt.PatchError as e:
                    rec.update(ok=False, stage="apply", reason=f"patch does not apply: {e}")
                    tracing.set_verdict(span, "does not apply")
            if "stage" not in rec:
                with tracing.worker("trueup-verifier", step=f"try {n}") as span:
                    rec.update(verify_try(root, clone, target, finding, draft, writes, base, out))
                    rec["stage"] = "verified" if rec["ok"] else "verify"
                    rec["diff"] = pt.diff(clone)
                    tracing.set_verdict(span, "pass" if rec["ok"] else "fail")
            out(f"try {n}: {'PASS' if rec['ok'] else 'FAIL'}: {_short(rec['reason'], 400)}")
            result["tries"].append(rec)
            if rec["ok"]:
                result["fixed"] = True
                write_fix(fix_dir, finding, target, base, rec)
                break
            messages = pt.revision_prompt(messages, draft, rec["reason"])
    except (ModelError, vf.VerifyError, RuntimeError) as e:

        out(f"fixer stopped: {result['error']}")
    finally:

            loc.reset_clone(clone)
        record_spend(run_dir, "after", client)
        spend = json.loads((run_dir / "spend.json").read_text())
        result["usage"], result["cost_usd"] = spend.get("usage"), spend.get("run_cost_usd")
        result["spend_after_usd"] = spend.get("after", {}).get("spend_usd")
        write_log(fix_dir, run_dir, result)
    out(f"{finding_id}: {'fixed, verified' if result['fixed'] else 'NOT fixed'} after {len(result['tries'])} "
        f"tr{'y' if len(result['tries']) == 1 else 'ies'}; model cost ${result['cost_usd']}; wrote {fix_dir}")
    return result

                            for p, s in t.get("suites", {}).items()} for n, t in

new='''def ensure_test_venv(root: Path, clone: Path, library: str, pkg: Package) -> Path:
    """One venv per package: packages of one repo can pin conflicting test requirements."""
    d = venvs.venv_dir(root, f"{library}-fixtest-{Path(pkg.path).name or library}")
    py = d / "bin" / "python"
    stamp = {"package": pkg.path, "local": list(pkg.local_deps), "deps": list(pkg.test_deps)}
    if py.exists() and (d / venvs.STAMP).exists() and json.loads((d / venvs.STAMP).read_text()) == stamp:
        return py
    _run([_uv(), "venv", "--quiet", "--allow-existing", "--python", "3.12", str(d)])
    # Local packages of the repo, editable, replace any PyPI release a test requirement pulls in.
    local = [*pkg.local_deps, pkg.path]
    _run([_uv(), "pip", "install", "--quiet", "--python", str(py), *test_requirements(clone, pkg),
          *(a for x in local for a in ("-e", str(clone / x)))])
    (d / venvs.STAMP).write_text(json.dumps(stamp))
    return py


'''

When the Agents SDK fires on_span_start for a GenerationSpanData/ResponseSpanData, _hooks.py creates an OTel LLM span and attaches it as the current context. The openai instrumentation's responses_get_or_create_wrapper then runs under that context and creates a second LLM span for the same call, doubling the count. The fix mirrors what LangChain/LiteLLM do: set SUPPRESS_LANGUAGE_MODEL_INSTRUMENTATION_KEY=True in the context when attaching the generation span, so the openai wrapper sees the suppression flag and skips creating its own span. +            self.tools = []
+
+    class FunctionSpanData(_Base):

+            self.name = name
+            self.input = None
+            self.output = None
+
+    class HandoffSpanData(_Base):
+        def __init__(self):
+            self.from_agent = "a"
+            self.to_agent = "b"
+
+    class TracingProcessor:
+        pass
+
+    agents_mod.AgentSpanData = AgentSpanData
+    agents_mod.GenerationSpanData = GenerationSpanData
+    agents_mod.FunctionSpanData = FunctionSpanData
+    agents_mod.HandoffSpanData = HandoffSpanData

+

+

content.content:
=== try 2 The root span's status is always set to OK in on_trace_end regardless of whether child spans had errors. The fix tracks per-trace whether any child span ended with an ERROR status, then uses that in on_trace_end. The test uses MaxTurnsExceeded by registering a real tool so the run loops until the turn limit, which causes the SDK to set span.error on the agent span.
--- a/python/instrumentation/openinference-instrumentation-openai-agents/src/openinference/instrumentation/openai_agents/_processor.py
+++ b/python/instrumentation/openinference-instrumentation-openai-agents/src/openinference/instrumentation/openai_agents/_processor.py
@@ -122,6 +122,7 @@ class OpenInferenceTracingProcessor(TracingProcessor):
+        self._trace_had_error: dict[str, bool] = {}
@@ -136,6 +137,7 @@ class OpenInferenceTracingProcessor(TracingProcessor):
+        self._trace_had_error[trace.trace_id] = False
@@ -144,8 +146,12 @@ class OpenInferenceTracingProcessor(TracingProcessor):
+        had_error = self._trace_had_error.pop(trace.trace_id, False)
-            root_span.set_status(Status(StatusCode.OK))
+            if had_error:
+                root_span.set_status(Status(StatusCode.ERROR))
+            else:
+                root_span.set_status(Status(StatusCode.OK))
@@ -261,7 +267,10 @@ class OpenInferenceTracingProcessor(TracingProcessor):
-        otel_span.set_status(status=_get_span_status(span))
+        span_status = _get_span_status(span)
+        otel_span.set_status(status=span_status)
+        if span_status.status_code == StatusCode.ERROR:

"""Where a finding's code lives in each library, and how that package runs its own tests.

A target is keyed by (library, code path) as the checker groups findings. It names
the packages in the library's repo the fix may touch, the symbols to start the
search from (the wrapper), the symbols that show how the library already gets a
similar case right, and the test requirements of each package.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field

REPOS = {
    "neatlogs": "https://github.com/neatlogs/neatlogs",
    "openinference": "https://github.com/Arize-ai/openinference",
    "openllmetry": "https://github.com/traceloop/openllmetry",
}
ISSUE_REPOS = {"neatlogs": "neatlogs/neatlogs", "openinference": "Arize-ai/openinference",
               "openllmetry": "traceloop/openllmetry"}


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Package:
    path: str  # in the repo
    dist: str  # distribution name, as installed in the scenario venv
    tests: str = "tests"  # relative to path
    # Test requirements: "group:<name>" reads [dependency-groups] of the package's pyproject,
    # "file:<name>" a requirements file in the package; anything else is a requirement.
    test_deps: tuple[str, ...] = ()
    # Local packages of the same repo the tests need from source (editable).
    local_deps: tuple[str, ...] = ()


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Target:
    library: str
    code_path: str
    packages: tuple[Package, ...]
    seeds: tuple[str, ...]  # wrapper functions or classes to locate
    reference_seeds: tuple[str, ...] = ()  # where the library gets a similar case right
    reference_note: str = ""  # the rule the fix must follow (OTel GenAI conventions)
    extra: dict[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict)


_OLL_SEMCONV = "packages/opentelemetry-semantic-conventions-ai"
_OLL_TEST = ("group:test", "group:dev")
_OI_CORE = ("python/openinference-semantic-conventions", "python/openinference-instrumentation")

TARGETS: dict[tuple[str, str], Target] = {
    ("openllmetry", "openai-agents"): Target(
        library="openllmetry", code_path="openai-agents",
        packages=(
            Package("packages/opentelemetry-instrumentation-openai-agents", "opentelemetry-instrumentation-openai-agents",
                    test_deps=_OLL_TEST, local_deps=(_OLL_SEMCONV, "packages/opentelemetry-instrumentation-openai")),
            Package("packages/opentelemetry-instrumentation-openai", "opentelemetry-instrumentation-openai",
                    test_deps=_OLL_TEST, local_deps=(_OLL_SEMCONV,)),
        ),
        seeds=("OpenTelemetryTracingProcessor", "on_span_start", "on_span_end", "responses_get_or_create_wrapper",
               "async_responses_get_or_create_wrapper"),
        reference_seeds=("SUPPRESS_LANGUAGE_MODEL_INSTRUMENTATION_KEY",),
        reference_note=("OTel GenAI conventions: one inference span per model call. OpenInference records the "
                        "same Agents SDK runs with one LLM span per call. Inside OpenLLMetry, the LangChain "
                        "instrumentation sets SUPPRESS_LANGUAGE_MODEL_INSTRUMENTATION_KEY in the context so the "
                        "provider instrumentation under it does not record the same call again."),
    ),
    ("openinference", "openai-agents"): Target(
        library="openinference", code_path="openai-agents",
        packages=(
            Package("python/instrumentation/openinference-instrumentation-openai-agents",
                    "openinference-instrumentation-openai-agents", test_deps=("file:test-requirements.txt", "pytest"),
                    local_deps=_OI_CORE),
        ),
        seeds=("OpenInferenceTracingProcessor", "on_trace_start", "on_trace_end", "on_span_end", "_get_span_status"),
        reference_note=("OTel conventions: a span whose operation failed has status ERROR. When an Agents SDK run "
                        "raises, the SDK attaches the error to the agent span (span.error); the inner span is "
                        "already ERROR in OpenInference. The root span covers the whole run, so it must not be OK "
                        "when the run failed. A run whose tool raised but which still finished must stay OK."),
    ),
    ("neatlogs", "anthropic messages stream"): Target(
        library="neatlogs", code_path="anthropic messages stream",
        packages=(Package(".", "neatlogs", test_deps=("pytest", "pytest-asyncio", "anthropic", "openai")),),
        seeds=("MessageStreamManager", "__exit__", "__aexit__", "stream"),
        reference_note=("OTel conventions: a span whose operation failed has status ERROR with an exception "
                        "event. neatlogs already does this for messages.create(stream=True)."),
    ),
}


def get(library: str, code_path: str) -> Target:

        return TARGETS[(library, code_path)]
    except KeyError:
        raise KeyError(f"no fix target for {library} / {code_path!r}; known: "
                       f"{', '.join(f'{a}/{b}' for a, b in TARGETS)}") from None

import pathlib
p=pathlib.Path('src/trueup/fixer/targets.py'); s=p.read_text()
old=s[s.index('    ("neatlogs", "anthropic messages stream"): Target('):s.index('}\n\n\ndef get')]
new='''    ("neatlogs", "anthropic messages stream"): Target(
        library="neatlogs", code_path="anthropic messages stream",
        packages=(Package(".", "neatlogs", tests="tests/unit", test_deps=("group:dev", "anthropic", "openai")),),
        seeds=("patched_stream", "_SyncStreamManagerWrapper", "_SyncStreamIterator", "_AsyncStreamManagerWrapper",
               "_AsyncStreamIterator", "_finalize_stream"),
        reference_seeds=("_err",),
        reference_note=("OTel conventions: a span whose operation failed has status ERROR with an exception "
                        "event. neatlogs already does this for messages.create(stream=True), through _err."),
    ),
'''
s=s.replace(old,new); p.write_text(s)
p=pathlib.Path('src/trueup/fix.py'); s=p.read_text()
old='''def find_finding(root: Path, finding_id: str) -> tuple[dict[str, Any], Path]:
    """The finding with this id in the newest findings.json that has it."""
    for f in sorted((root / ".trueup" / "runs").glob("*/findings.json"), reverse=True):
        for x in json.loads(f.read_text())["findings"]:
            if x["id"] == finding_id:
                return x, f.parent
    raise FileNotFoundError(f"no finding {finding_id!r} in .trueup/runs/*/findings.json")'''
new='''def find_finding(root: Path, finding_id: str) -> tuple[dict[str, Any], Path]:
    """The finding with this id, from the newest findings.json that has it. The id names the library,
    check, field and code path, so the same id in other checked runs (other scenarios, such as
    planner proposals) is the same finding: their scenarios and leads are added to it."""
    found: list[tuple[dict[str, Any], Path]] = []
    for f in sorted((root / ".trueup" / "runs").glob("*/findings.json"), reverse=True):
        found += [(x, f.parent) for x in json.loads(f.read_text())["findings"] if x["id"] == finding_id]
    if not found:
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"no finding {finding_id!r} in .trueup/runs/*/findings.json")
    finding, run_dir = json.loads(json.dumps(found[0][0])), found[0][1]
    d = finding["details"]
    d["runs"] = {sid: run_dir.name for sid in d["scenarios"]}
    for other, odir in found[1:]:
        for sid in other["details"]["scenarios"]:
            if sid not in d["scenarios"]:
                d["scenarios"].append(sid)
                d["runs"][sid] = odir.name
        d["leads"] += [m for m in other["details"].get("leads", []) if m["scenario"] not in
                       {x["scenario"] for x in d["leads"]}]
    return finding, run_dir'''
assert old in s; s=s.replace(old,new); p.write_text(s)
EOF
