def run_repro(py: Path, script: str, timeout: float = 180) -> dict[str, Any]:
    env = vf.test_env()
    env.pop("OPENAI_API_KEY", None)  # the Agents SDK's own exporter then skips its upload
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="trueup-upstream-") as tmp:
        f = Path(tmp) / "repro.py"
        f.write_text(script)
        try:
            p = subprocess.run([str(py), str(f)], cwd=tmp, env=env, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout)
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
            return {"exit": -1, "stdout": "", "stderr": f"timed out after {timeout:.0f} s"}
    return {"exit": p.returncode, "stdout": p.stdout.strip(), "stderr": p.stderr.strip()[-1500:]}


def versions(py: Path, library: str) -> dict[str, str]:
    code = ("import json, importlib.metadata as m\nout = {}\nfor d in " + json.dumps(VERSIONED[library]) +
            ":\n    try: out[d] = m.version(d)\n    except Exception: pass\nprint(json.dumps(out))")
    p = subprocess.run([str(py), "-c", code], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=60)
    return json.loads(p.stdout) if p.returncode == 0 else {}


def boundary(finding: dict[str, Any], fix_dir: Path) -> dict[str, list[str]]:
    """Scenarios on the same code path (id prefix) that are right before the patch, from the fix's baseline."""
    base = json.loads((fix_dir / "baseline.json").read_text())["sweep"] if (fix_dir / "baseline.json").exists() \
        else {"leads": {}}
    d = finding["details"]
    prefixes = tuple({sid.split("-", 1)[0] + "-" for sid in d["scenarios"]})
    same = [sid for sid in base["leads"] if sid.startswith(prefixes)]
    right = [sid for sid in same if sid not in d["scenarios"] and not any(
        vf.matches_finding(m, finding) for m in base["leads"][sid])]
    return {"affected": d["scenarios"], "right": right}


def patched_python(root: Path, target: tg.Target, fix_dir: Path) -> tuple[Path | None, str]:
    """The -fix venv with patch.diff applied to the clean clone and installed. (None, reason) if no fix."""
    diff = fix_dir / "patch.diff"
    if not diff.exists():
        return None, "no verified fix in fixes/ for this finding"
    clone, _ = loc.ensure_clone(root, target.library)
    loc.reset_clone(clone)
    p = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(clone), "apply", str(diff.resolve())], capture_output=True, text=True)
    if p.returncode != 0:
        loc.reset_clone(clone)
        return None, f"patch.diff does not apply to the clone: {p.stderr.strip()[-300:]}"
    try:
        py = venvs.venv_dir(root, f"{target.library}-fix") / "bin" / "python"
        if not py.exists():
            py = vf.ensure_fix_venv(root, clone, target.library)
        vf.reinstall(py, clone, target)
    finally:
        loc.reset_clone(clone)
    return py, "patched"


def upstream(root: Path, finding_id: str, out: Any = print) -> Path:

def run_repro(py: Path, script: str, timeout: float = 180) -> dict[str, Any]:

        try:
            p = subprocess.run([str(py), str(f)], cwd=tmp, env=env, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout)
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
            return {"exit": -1, "stdout": "", "stderr": f"timed out after {timeout:.0f} s"}
    return {"exit": p.returncode, "stdout": p.stdout.strip(), "stderr": p.stderr.strip()[-1500:]}

    p = subprocess.run([str(py), "-c", code], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=60)

"""trueup upstream <finding-id>: draft issue and PR text into upstream/<finding-id>/. Never posts.

The text is built from recorded data: the finding, the fix's before/after table and suite results
(fixes/<id>/), the scenarios on the same code path that are right (the boundary), and a standalone
repro that needs only the library and the provider SDK (httpx.MockTransport answers; no keys, no
network). The repro is run here, on the latest release and on the clone with patch.diff applied,
and its output goes into the text. The issue follows the repo's issue template when it has one.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import platform
import subprocess
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

from trueup.core.repro import line_count
from trueup.fix import find_finding
from trueup.fixer import locate as loc
from trueup.fixer import targets as tg
from trueup.fixer import verify as vf
from trueup.runner import venvs
from trueup.runner.setups import VERSIONED

MAX_REPRO_LINES = 40

_AGENTS_BODY = '''BODY = {"id": "resp_1", "object": "response", "created_at": 0, "status": "completed", "model": "m",
        "output": [{"type": "message", "id": "msg_1", "role": "assistant", "status": "completed",
                    "content": [{"type": "output_text", "text": "Hello!", "annotations": []}]}],
        "parallel_tool_calls": True, "tool_choice": "auto", "tools": [],
        "usage": {"input_tokens": 11, "output_tokens": 7, "total_tokens": 18,
                  "input_tokens_details": {"cached_tokens": 0}, "output_tokens_details": {"reasoning_tokens": 0}}}'''

REPROS: dict[tuple[str, str], str] = {
    ("openllmetry", "openai-agents"): '''"""OpenLLMetry + OpenAI Agents SDK: one model call is recorded as two LLM spans.
Needs traceloop-sdk and openai-agents. Offline: httpx.MockTransport answers. Leave OPENAI_API_KEY
unset so the Agents SDK's own exporter skips its upload."""
import asyncio

import httpx
from openai import AsyncOpenAI
from opentelemetry.sdk.trace.export.in_memory_span_exporter import InMemorySpanExporter
from traceloop.sdk import Traceloop

exporter = InMemorySpanExporter()
Traceloop.init(app_name="repro", exporter=exporter, disable_batch=True, telemetry_enabled=False)
from agents import Agent, OpenAIResponsesModel, Runner  # noqa: E402

''' + _AGENTS_BODY + '''
transport = httpx.MockTransport(lambda request: httpx.Response(200, json=BODY))
client = AsyncOpenAI(api_key="x", base_url="http://fake/v1", http_client=httpx.AsyncClient(transport=transport))
agent = Agent(name="helper", model=OpenAIResponsesModel("m", client))
asyncio.run(Runner.run(agent, "hi"))
llm = [s for s in exporter.get_finished_spans() if s.attributes.get("gen_ai.operation.name") == "chat"]
tokens = sum(s.attributes.get("gen_ai.usage.output_tokens", 0) for s in llm)
print(f"provider requests: 1; LLM spans: {len(llm)}; output tokens on LLM spans: {tokens} (provider sent 7)")
''',
    ("openinference", "openai-agents"): '''"""OpenInference + OpenAI Agents SDK: a run that raises leaves the top-level span OK.
Needs openinference-instrumentation-openai-agents and openai-agents. Offline: httpx.MockTransport
answers HTTP 500. Leave OPENAI_API_KEY unset so the Agents SDK's own exporter skips its upload."""
import asyncio

import httpx
from openai import AsyncOpenAI
from openinference.instrumentation.openai_agents import OpenAIAgentsInstrumentor
from opentelemetry.sdk.trace import TracerProvider
from opentelemetry.sdk.trace.export import SimpleSpanProcessor
from opentelemetry.sdk.trace.export.in_memory_span_exporter import InMemorySpanExporter

exporter = InMemorySpanExporter()
provider = TracerProvider()
provider.add_span_processor(SimpleSpanProcessor(exporter))
OpenAIAgentsInstrumentor().instrument(tracer_provider=provider)
from agents import Agent, OpenAIResponsesModel, Runner  # noqa: E402

transport = httpx.MockTransport(lambda request: httpx.Response(500, json={"error": {"message": "boom"}}))
client = AsyncOpenAI(api_key="x", base_url="http://fake/v1", max_retries=0,
                     http_client=httpx.AsyncClient(transport=transport))
agent = Agent(name="helper", model=OpenAIResponsesModel("m", client))
try:
    asyncio.run(Runner.run(agent, "hi"))
except Exception as e:
    print(f"the run raised {type(e).__name__}")
root = next(s for s in exporter.get_finished_spans() if s.parent is None)
print(f"top-level span {root.name!r}: {root.status.status_code.name}")
''',
    ("neatlogs", "anthropic messages stream"): '''"""neatlogs + Anthropic messages.stream(): a stream that fails leaves the span OK.
Needs neatlogs and anthropic. Offline: httpx.MockTransport answers with an SSE stream that ends in an

import json

import anthropic
import httpx
import neatlogs
from opentelemetry.sdk.trace import TracerProvider
from opentelemetry.sdk.trace.export import SimpleSpanProcessor
from opentelemetry.sdk.trace.export.in_memory_span_exporter import InMemorySpanExporter

exporter, provider = InMemorySpanExporter(), TracerProvider()
neatlogs.init(api_key="x", instrumentations=["anthropic"], disable_export=True, tracer_provider=provider)
provider.add_span_processor(SimpleSpanProcessor(exporter))
start = {"type": "message_start", "message": {"id": "msg_1", "type": "message", "role": "assistant", "model": "m",
         "content": [], "stop_reason": None, "usage": {"input_tokens": 5, "output_tokens": 0}}}
error = {"type": "error", "error": {"type": "overloaded_error", "message": "Overloaded"}}
sse = "".join(f"event: {e['type']}\\ndata: {json.dumps(e)}\\n\\n" for e in (start, error))
transport = httpx.MockTransport(lambda r: httpx.Response(200, text=sse, headers={"content-type": "text/event-stream"}))
client = anthropic.Anthropic(api_key="x", base_url="http://fake", http_client=httpx.Client(transport=transport))
try:
    with client.messages.stream(model="m", max_tokens=16, messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}]) as s:
        "".join(s.text_stream)
except Exception as e:
    print(f"the app saw {type(e).__name__}")
neatlogs.flush()
for span in exporter.get_finished_spans():
    print(f"span {span.name!r}: {span.status.status_code.name}, exception events: "
          f"{sum(e.name == 'exception' for e in span.events)}")
''',
}

# Per library: the template's component, the PR title prefix and the issue template file.
META = {
    ("openllmetry", "openai-agents"): {
        "component": "OpenAI Instrumentation", "pr_title": "fix(openai-agents): record one LLM span per model call",
        "title": "OpenAI Agents SDK: every non-streamed model call is recorded as two LLM spans (calls and tokens "
                 "doubled)"},
    ("openinference", "openai-agents"): {
        "pr_title": "fix(openai-agents): set the root span to ERROR when the agent run fails",
        "title": "openai-agents: a run that raises leaves the top-level span OK"},
    ("neatlogs", "anthropic messages stream"): {
        "pr_title": "fix(anthropic): record an error on messages.stream() spans when the stream fails",
        "title": "Anthropic messages.stream(): a stream that fails (error event or cut connection) is recorded as OK"},
}


def run_repro(py: Path, script: str, timeout: float = 180) -> dict[str, Any]:
    env = vf.test_env()
    env.pop("OPENAI_API_KEY", None)  # the Agents SDK's own exporter then skips its upload
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="trueup-upstream-") as tmp:
        f = Path(tmp) / "repro.py"
        f.write_text(script)
        try:
            p = subprocess.run([str(py), str(f)], cwd=tmp, env=env, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout)
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
            return {"exit": -1, "stdout": "", "stderr": f"timed out after {timeout:.0f} s"}
    return {"exit": p.returncode, "stdout": p.stdout.strip(), "stderr": p.stderr.strip()[-1500:]}


def versions(py: Path, library: str) -> dict[str, str]:
    code = ("import json, importlib.metadata as m\nout = {}\nfor d in " + json.dumps(VERSIONED[library]) +
            ":\n    try: out[d] = m.version(d)\n    except Exception: pass\nprint(json.dumps(out))")
    p = subprocess.run([str(py), "-c", code], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=60)
    return json.loads(p.stdout) if p.returncode == 0 else {}


def boundary(finding: dict[str, Any], fix_dir: Path) -> dict[str, list[str]]:
    """Scenarios on the same code path (id prefix) that are right before the patch, from the fix's baseline."""
    base = json.loads((fix_dir / "baseline.json").read_text())["sweep"] if (fix_dir / "baseline.json").exists() \
        else {"leads": {}}
    d = finding["details"]
    prefixes = tuple({sid.split("-", 1)[0] + "-" for sid in d["scenarios"]})
    same = [sid for sid in base["leads"] if sid.startswith(prefixes)]
    right = [sid for sid in same if sid not in d["scenarios"] and not any(
        vf.matches_finding(m, finding) for m in base["leads"][sid])]
    return {"affected": d["scenarios"], "right": right}


def patched_python(root: Path, target: tg.Target, fix_dir: Path) -> tuple[Path | None, str]:
    """The -fix venv with patch.diff applied to the clean clone and installed. (None, reason) if no fix."""
    diff = fix_dir / "patch.diff"
    if not diff.exists():
        return None, "no verified fix in fixes/ for this finding"
    clone, _ = loc.ensure_clone(root, target.library)
    loc.reset_clone(clone)
    p = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(clone), "apply", str(diff.resolve())], capture_output=True, text=True)
    if p.returncode != 0:
        loc.reset_clone(clone)
        return None, f"patch.diff does not apply to the clone: {p.stderr.strip()[-300:]}"
    try:
        py = venvs.venv_dir(root, f"{target.library}-fix") / "bin" / "python"
        if not py.exists():
            py = vf.ensure_fix_venv(root, clone, target.library)
        vf.reinstall(py, clone, target)
    finally:
        loc.reset_clone(clone)
    return py, "patched"


def upstream(root: Path, finding_id: str, out: Any = print) -> Path:
    finding, _ = find_finding(root, finding_id)
    key = (finding["library"], finding["details"]["code_path"])
    target = tg.get(*key)
    script = REPROS[key]
    n = line_count(script)
    if n >= MAX_REPRO_LINES:
        raise ValueError(f"the repro has {n} lines; it must be under {MAX_REPRO_LINES}")
    fix_dir = root / "fixes" / finding_id
    up_dir = root / "upstream" / finding_id
    up_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    fix = json.loads((fix_dir / "tries.json").read_text()) if (fix_dir / "tries.json").exists() else None
    out("running the repro on the latest release")
    before_py = venvs.ensure(root, target.library)
    before = run_repro(before_py, script)
    after_py, why = patched_python(root, target, fix_dir) if fix and fix.get("fixed") else (None, "no verified fix")
    out(f"running the repro on the patched clone ({why})")
    after = run_repro(after_py, script) if after_py else None
    env = {"python": platform.python_version(), "os": f"{platform.system()} {platform.machine()}",
           "latest release": versions(before_py, target.library),
           "patched": {"commit": fix.get("commit") if fix else None, "packages": [p.path for p in target.packages]}}
    data = {"finding": finding_id, "repro_lines": n, "before": before, "after": after, "after_note": why,
            "environment": env, "boundary": boundary(finding, fix_dir), "fixed": bool(fix and fix.get("fixed")),
            "posted": False}
    (up_dir / "repro.py").write_text(script)
    (up_dir / "repro-output.json").write_text(json.dumps(data, indent=1))
    (up_dir / "issue.md").write_text(issue_text(root, finding, target, data, fix_dir))
    (up_dir / "pr.md").write_text(pr_text(finding, target, data, fix_dir, fix))
    out(f"repro ({n} lines) before: {before['stdout'] or before['stderr'][-200:]}")
    if after:
        out(f"repro after the patch: {after['stdout'] or after['stderr'][-200:]}")
    out(f"wrote {up_dir} (nothing posted)")
    return up_dir


def _code(text: str, lang: str = "") -> str:
    return f"```{lang}\n{text.rstrip()}\n```"


def _sections(finding: dict[str, Any], target: tg.Target, data: dict[str, Any], fix_dir: Path) -> dict[str, str]:
    d = finding["details"]
    b = data["boundary"]
    table = (fix_dir / "before-after.md").read_text() if (fix_dir / "before-after.md").exists() else ""
    rows = "\n".join(f"- `{x['scenario']}`: {x['field']} should be {x['truth']}, the trace has {x['trace']}"
                     for x in d.get("leads", []))
    return {
        "symptom": (f"{META[(target.library, target.code_path)]['title']}.\n\nTrueup ran each case against a fake "
                    f"provider, so it knows what really happened, and compared that with the exported spans:\n\n"
                    f"{rows}"),
        "boundary": (f"Affected: {', '.join(f'`{s}`' for s in b['affected'])}.\n\nRight today on the same code "
                     f"path: {', '.join(f'`{s}`' for s in b['right']) or 'none'}.\n\nReproduces on the latest "
                     f"release and on main ({d.get('rules', {}).get('latest_and_main', '')})."),
        "repro": (f"Standalone, {data['repro_lines']} lines, needs only the library and the SDK; no API key, no "
                  f"network:\n\n{_code(REPROS[(target.library, target.code_path)], 'python')}\n\nOutput on the "
                  f"latest release:\n\n{_code(data['before']['stdout'] or data['before']['stderr'])}"),
        "expected": target.reference_note,
        "table": table,
        "environment": (f"Python {data['environment']['python']}, {data['environment']['os']}. Versions: " +
                        ", ".join(f"{k} {v}" for k, v in data["environment"]["latest release"].items()) + "."),
        "dedupe": "; ".join(f"`{s['query']}` ({s['hits']} hits, {s['date'][:10]})"
                            for s in finding.get("dedupe", {}).get("searches", [])),

            f"**Additional context**\n\nBefore and after the proposed fix, from Trueup's runs:\n\n{s['table']}\n"
            f"Searched issues and PRs first: {s['dedupe']}."])
    return note + "\n\n".join([  # neatlogs has no issue template
        f"# {meta['title']}", f"## Symptom\n\n{s['symptom']}", f"## Boundary\n\n{s['boundary']}",
        f"## Repro\n\n{s['repro']}", f"## Expected\n\n{s['expected']}",
        f"## Before and after the proposed fix\n\n{s['table']}", f"## Environment\n\n{s['environment']}",
        f"Searched issues and PRs first: {s['dedupe']}."])

    after = data["after"]["stdout"] if data["after"] else "(not run)"

# [bug] openai-agents: a run that raises leaves the top-level span OK

**Describe the bug**

openai-agents: a run that raises leaves the top-level span OK.

Trueup ran each case against a fake provider, so it knows what really happened, and compared that with the exported spans:

- `ag-llm-fails`: top-level span status should be ERROR (app raised InternalServerError), the trace has OK
- `ag-max-turns`: top-level span status should be ERROR (app raised MaxTurnsExceeded), the trace has OK
- `ag-bad-tool`: top-level span status should be ERROR (app raised ModelBehaviorError), the trace has OK
- `ag-streamed-error`: top-level span status should be ERROR (app raised ModelBehaviorError), the trace has OK
- `ag-streamed-cut`: top-level span status should be ERROR (app raised APIConnectionError), the trace has OK

Affected: `ag-bad-tool`, `ag-llm-fails`, `ag-max-turns`, `ag-streamed-cut`, `ag-streamed-error`.

Right today on the same code path: `ag-run`, `ag-tool-raises`, `ag-streamed`.

Reproduces on the latest release and on main (latest release and main c364180e5b).

**To Reproduce**

Standalone, 28 lines, needs only the library and the SDK; no API key, no network:

```python
"""OpenInference + OpenAI Agents SDK: a run that raises leaves the top-level span OK.
Needs openinference-instrumentation-openai-agents and openai-agents. Offline: httpx.MockTransport
answers HTTP 500. Leave OPENAI_API_KEY unset so the Agents SDK's own exporter skips its upload."""
import asyncio

import httpx
from openai import AsyncOpenAI
from openinference.instrumentation.openai_agents import OpenAIAgentsInstrumentor
from opentelemetry.sdk.trace import TracerProvider
from opentelemetry.sdk.trace.export import SimpleSpanProcessor
from opentelemetry.sdk.trace.export.in_memory_span_exporter import InMemorySpanExporter

exporter = InMemorySpanExporter()
provider = TracerProvider()
provider.add_span_processor(SimpleSpanProcessor(exporter))
OpenAIAgentsInstrumentor().instrument(tracer_provider=provider)
from agents import Agent, OpenAIResponsesModel, Runner  # noqa: E402

transport = httpx.MockTransport(lambda request: httpx.Response(500, json={"error": {"message": "boom"}}))
client = AsyncOpenAI(api_key="x", base_url="http://fake/v1", max_retries=0,
                     http_client=httpx.AsyncClient(transport=transport))
agent = Agent(name="helper", model=OpenAIResponsesModel("m", client))
try:
    asyncio.run(Runner.run(agent, "hi"))
except Exception as e:
    print(f"the run raised {type(e).__name__}")
root = next(s for s in exporter.get_finished_spans() if s.parent is None)
print(f"top-level span {root.name!r}: {root.status.status_code.name}")
```

Output on the latest release:

```
the run raised InternalServerError
top-level span 'Agent workflow': OK
```

**Expected behavior**

OTel conventions: a span whose operation failed has status ERROR. The root span covers the whole run, so it must not be OK when the run raised. Which SDK span carries the error differs by failure (the agent span, a turn span or a response span; see the spans below). A run whose tool raised but which still finished must stay OK: the SDK marks that function span with a non-fatal error.

**Screenshots**

None; the repro prints the span status.

**Environment**

Python 3.12.3, Linux x86_64. Versions: openinference-instrumentation-openai 0.1.65, openinference-instrumentation-anthropic 3.0.3, openinference-instrumentation-langchain 0.1.79, openinference-instrumentation-openai-agents 2.5.3, openai 3.28.0, anthropic 1.13.0, opentelemetry-sdk 1.45.1, langchain-core 1.6.9, langchain-openai 1.7.0, langgraph 1.2.14, openai-agents 0.23.1.

**Additional context**

Before and after the proposed fix, from Trueup's runs:

<!-- Drafted by Trueup from recorded runs. Not posted. -->

# fix(openai-agents): record one LLM span per model call

## What

When both openai-agents and openai instrumentations are active, each LLM call produces two spans: one from the agents processor's _start_generation_span and one from responses_get_or_create_wrapper. The fix sets SUPPRESS_LANGUAGE_MODEL_INSTRUMENTATION_KEY=True in the context when the agents processor attaches a generation/response span (exactly as LangChain and LiteLLM do), and adds a check for that key in both sync and async responses wrappers so they skip creating a duplicate span.

## Files

- `packages/opentelemetry-instrumentation-openai-agents/opentelemetry/instrumentation/openai_agents/_hooks.py`
- `packages/opentelemetry-instrumentation-openai-agents/tests/test_trueup_llm_span_dedup.py`
- `packages/opentelemetry-instrumentation-openai/opentelemetry/instrumentation/openai/v1/responses_wrappers.py`

## Test

new test: fails before (1 failing), passes after (4 passed).

## Suites

- `packages/opentelemetry-instrumentation-openai-agents` before the patch: 405 passed, 1 failing (test_none_finish_reason_omits_attribute)
- `packages/opentelemetry-instrumentation-openai` before the patch: 291 passed, 0 failing
- `packages/opentelemetry-instrumentation-openai-agents`: same 1 failure(s) as before the patch
- `packages/opentelemetry-instrumentation-openai`: suite passes

## Before and after

| scenario | field | truth | before | after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ag-bad-tool | LLM spans | 1 (provider requests) | 2 | matches truth |

"""Offline tests for the fixer, the verifier rules and the upstream drafts."""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from trueup import tracing
from trueup.cli import build_parser
from trueup.core.repro import line_count
from trueup.fix import find_finding
from trueup.fixer import locate as loc
from trueup.fixer import patch as pt
from trueup.fixer import targets as tg
from trueup.fixer import verify as vf
from trueup import upstream as up

TARGET = tg.Target(library="lib", code_path="x", packages=(tg.Package("pkg", "pkg"),), seeds=("wrap",),
                   reference_seeds=("KEY",))


@pytest.fixture
def repo(tmp_path: Path) -> Path:
    (tmp_path / "pkg" / "lib").mkdir(parents=True)
    (tmp_path / "pkg" / "tests").mkdir()
    (tmp_path / "pkg" / "lib" / "w.py").write_text(
        "KEY = 1\n\n\nclass P:\n    def wrap(self, x):\n        return x\n\n    def use(self):\n"
        "        return self.wrap(1)\n\n\ndef top():\n    return P().wrap(2)\n")
    (tmp_path / "build" / "lib").mkdir(parents=True)
    (tmp_path / "build" / "lib" / "w.py").write_text("def wrap():\n    pass\n")
    return tmp_path


def draft(**kw):
    d = {"edits": [{"file": "pkg/lib/w.py", "old": "        return x\n", "new": "        return x + 1\n"}],
         "test": {"file": "pkg/tests/test_trueup_w.py", "content": "def test_x():\n    assert True\n"}}
    d.update(kw)
    return d


def test_check_draft_applies_and_returns_writes(repo: Path) -> None:
    writes = pt.check_draft(draft(), repo, TARGET)
    assert writes == [{"file": "pkg/lib/w.py", "content": (repo / "pkg/lib/w.py").read_text().replace(
        "return x\n", "return x + 1\n")}]


@pytest.mark.parametrize("edits, reason", [
    ([{"file": "other/w.py", "old": "a", "new": "b"}], "outside"),
    ([{"file": "build/lib/w.py", "old": "pass", "new": "x"}], "outside"),
    ([{"file": "pkg/tests/test_a.py", "old": "a", "new": "b"}], "outside"),
    ([{"file": "pkg/lib/w.py", "old": "    return x\n", "new": ""}], "found 0 times"),  # indentation differs
    ([{"file": "pkg/lib/w.py", "old": "wrap(", "new": "w("}], "found 3 times"),
    ([{"file": "pkg/lib/w.py", "old": "        return x\n", "new": "        return (\n"}], "does not compile"),
    ([], "non-empty"),
])
def test_check_draft_refuses(repo: Path, edits: list, reason: str) -> None:
    with pytest.raises(pt.PatchError, match=reason):
        pt.check_draft(draft(edits=edits), repo, TARGET)


def test_check_draft_shows_the_nearest_real_lines(repo: Path) -> None:
    with pytest.raises(pt.PatchError, match="really has, from line 5"):
        pt.check_draft(draft(edits=[{"file": "pkg/lib/w.py", "old": "    def wrap(self, y):\n", "new": ""}]),
                       repo, TARGET)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("test_file", ["pkg/lib/test_trueup_w.py", "pkg/tests/test_w.py", "pkg/tests/x.txt"])
def test_check_draft_test_file_must_be_new_trueup_test_in_tests(repo: Path, test_file: str) -> None:
    with pytest.raises(pt.PatchError, match="test file"):
        pt.check_draft(draft(test={"file": test_file, "content": "x = 1\n"}), repo, TARGET)


def test_locate_finds_definitions_callers_and_reference_skipping_build(repo: Path) -> None:
    found = loc.locate_symbols(repo, TARGET)
    assert [(d["file"], d["qualname"]) for d in found["definitions"]] == [("pkg/lib/w.py", "P.wrap")]
    assert sorted(c["in"] for c in found["callers"]) == ["P.use", "top"]
    assert all(not r["file"].startswith("build/") for r in found["callers"] + found["reference"])


def test_source_excerpt_is_verbatim(repo: Path) -> None:
    found = loc.locate_symbols(repo, TARGET)
    text = loc.source_excerpts(repo, found, limit=10)  # forces the excerpt path
    assert "    def wrap(self, x):\n        return x" in text
    assert "5: " not in text  # no line-number prefixes the model could copy into an edit


def test_probe_graph_records_why_it_was_not_used(repo: Path, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:
    import subprocess

    monkeypatch.setattr(loc.shutil, "which", lambda name: "/bin/" + name)

    def run(cmd, cwd, timeout):
        missing = cmd[1] == "graph"
        return subprocess.CompletedProcess(cmd, 1 if missing else 0, "" if missing else "help",
                                           "the entire-graph plugin is not installed" if missing else "")

    rec = loc.probe_graph(repo, ("wrap",), run)
    assert rec["used"] is False and "not installed" in rec["reason"] and len(rec["commands"]) == 3


JUNIT = """<?xml version="1.0"?><testsuites><testsuite name="pytest">
<testcase classname="tests.test_a" name="test_ok"/><testcase classname="tests.test_a" name="test_bad"><failure/></testcase>
<testcase classname="tests.test_b" name="test_skip"><skipped/></testcase>
<testcase classname="" name="tests.test_c"><error/></testcase></testsuite></testsuites>"""


def test_parse_junit(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    (tmp_path / "j.xml").write_text(JUNIT)
    r = vf.parse_junit(tmp_path / "j.xml")
    assert (r["total"], r["passed"], r["failed"], r["errors"], r["skipped"]) == (4, 1, 1, 1, 1)
    assert r["failing"] == ["::tests.test_c", "tests.test_a::test_bad"]


def suite(failing: list[str], total: int = 10, exit: int = 1, passed: int = 9) -> dict:
    return {"failing": failing, "total": total, "exit": exit, "passed": passed, "tail": "", "tests": []}


def test_suite_verdict() -> None:
    before = suite(["a::old"])
    assert vf.suite_verdict(before, suite(["a::old"], total=11), "tests/test_trueup_x.py") == (
        True, "same 1 failure(s) as before the patch")
    assert vf.suite_verdict(before, suite([], total=11), None)[0]
    ok, why = vf.suite_verdict(before, suite(["a::old", "a::new"], total=11), None)
    assert not ok and "a::new" in why
    assert not vf.suite_verdict(before, suite([], total=5), None)[0]  # fewer tests ran
    assert not vf.suite_verdict(before, {"exit": 2, "tail": "boom"}, None)[0]


def test_baseline_must_really_run() -> None:
    assert vf.baseline_usable(suite([], exit=0))[0]
    assert not vf.baseline_usable(suite(["x"], total=1, exit=2, passed=0))[0]  # collection interrupted
    assert not vf.baseline_usable({"exit": -1, "tail": "timed out"})[0]


def test_new_test_verdict_and_weak_tests() -> None:
    before = {"total": 2, "failing": ["m::test_a"], "tests": ["m::test_a", "m::test_b"], "exit": 1, "tail": ""}
    ok, why = vf.new_test_verdict(before, {"total": 2, "failing": [], "exit": 0, "tail": ""})
    assert ok and "test_b" in why and "do not show the bug" in why
    assert not vf.new_test_verdict({**before, "failing": []}, {"total": 2, "failing": [], "exit": 0, "tail": ""})[0]
    assert not vf.new_test_verdict(before, {"total": 2, "failing": ["m::test_a"], "exit": 1, "tail": ""})[0]
    assert not vf.new_test_verdict({"total": 0, "exit": 4, "tail": ""}, {"total": 1, "failing": []})[0]


FINDING = {"id": "f", "details": {"check": "run_status", "field": "status", "scenarios": ["ag-a", "ag-b"]}}


def lead(check: str = "run_status", field: str = "status", truth: str = "ERROR", trace: str = "OK") -> dict:
    return {"check": check, "field": field, "truth": truth, "trace": trace, "severity": "high"}


def test_scenario_verdict_new_mismatches_and_table() -> None:
    before = {"leads": {"ag-a": [lead()], "ag-b": [lead(), lead("tokens", "t", 1, 2)], "ag-c": []}, "not_run": {}}
    after = {"leads": {"ag-a": [], "ag-b": [lead("tokens", "t", 1, 2)], "ag-c": [lead(truth="OK", trace="ERROR")]},
             "not_run": {}, "spans": {}}
    assert vf.scenario_verdict(after, FINDING)[0]
    new = vf.new_mismatches(before, after)
    assert [(m["scenario"], m["trace"]) for m in new] == [("ag-c", "ERROR")]
    still = {"leads": {"ag-a": [lead()], "ag-b": []}, "not_run": {}, "spans": {"ag-a": [["root", "OK", "", None]]}}
    ok, why = vf.scenario_verdict(still, FINDING)
    assert not ok and "ag-a: truth ERROR, trace OK" in why and "root" in why
    assert not vf.scenario_verdict({"leads": {"ag-a": []}, "not_run": {}}, FINDING)[0]
    rows = vf.before_after(FINDING, before, after)
    assert rows[0] == {"scenario": "ag-a", "field": "status", "truth": "ERROR", "before": "OK",
                       "after": "matches truth"}
    assert "| before | 3 | 0 | 3 |" in vf.table_md(rows, vf.totals(before), vf.totals(after))


def test_test_requirements_reads_groups_and_files(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    (tmp_path / "p").mkdir()
    (tmp_path / "p" / "pyproject.toml").write_text('[dependency-groups]\ntest = ["pytest>=8", {include-group = "x"}]\n')
    (tmp_path / "p" / "req.txt").write_text("respx  # mock\n-e ../x\n\nvcrpy\n")
    pkg = tg.Package("p", "p", test_deps=("group:test", "file:req.txt", "extra"))
    assert vf.test_requirements(tmp_path, pkg) == ["pytest>=8", "respx", "vcrpy", "extra"]


def test_test_env_drops_every_key(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:
    for k in ("TRUEUP_MODEL_KEY", "NEATLOGS_API_KEY", "OPENAI_API_KEY", "GH_TOKEN", "VIRTUAL_ENV"):
        monkeypatch.setenv(k, "v")
    env = vf.test_env()
    assert not {"TRUEUP_MODEL_KEY", "NEATLOGS_API_KEY", "OPENAI_API_KEY", "GH_TOKEN", "VIRTUAL_ENV"} & set(env)


def write_findings(root: Path, run: str, scenarios: list[str]) -> None:
    d = root / ".trueup" / "runs" / run
    d.mkdir(parents=True)
    leads = [{**lead(), "scenario": s} for s in scenarios]
    (d / "findings.json").write_text(json.dumps({"findings": [
        {"id": "f", "library": "neatlogs", "details": {**FINDING["details"], "scenarios": scenarios, "leads": leads}}]}))


def test_find_finding_merges_the_same_id_across_runs(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    write_findings(tmp_path, "20261010T1-neatlogs-proposed", ["p-an-a"])
    write_findings(tmp_path, "20261010T2-neatlogs-proposed", ["p-an-b", "p-an-a"])
    f, run_dir = find_finding(tmp_path, "f")
    assert run_dir.name == "20261010T2-neatlogs-proposed"
    assert f["details"]["scenarios"] == ["p-an-b", "p-an-a"]
    assert f["details"]["runs"]["p-an-a"] == "20261010T2-neatlogs-proposed"
    with pytest.raises(FileNotFoundError):
        find_finding(tmp_path, "nope")


def test_code_path_prefix() -> None:
    assert pt.code_path_prefix("ag-run") == "ag-"
    assert pt.code_path_prefix("p-an-stream-helper-cut") == "p-an-"


def test_every_target_has_a_short_standalone_repro_and_meta() -> None:
    assert set(up.REPROS) == set(tg.TARGETS) == set(up.META)
    for key, script in up.REPROS.items():
        assert line_count(script) < up.MAX_REPRO_LINES, key
        assert "trueup" not in script  # standalone: the library and the SDK only

    (d / "findings.json").write_text(json.dumps({"findings": [
        {"id": "f", "library": "neatlogs", "details": {**FINDING["details"], "scenarios": scenarios, "leads": leads}}]}))


def test_find_finding_merges_the_same_id_across_runs(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    write_findings(tmp_path, "20261010T1-neatlogs-proposed", ["p-an-a"])
    write_findings(tmp_path, "20261010T2-neatlogs-proposed", ["p-an-b", "p-an-a"])
    f, run_dir = find_finding(tmp_path, "f")
    assert run_dir.name == "20261010T2-neatlogs-proposed"
    assert f["details"]["scenarios"] == ["p-an-b", "p-an-a"]
    assert f["details"]["runs"]["p-an-a"] == "20261010T2-neatlogs-proposed"
    with pytest.raises(FileNotFoundError):
        find_finding(tmp_path, "nope")


def test_code_path_prefix() -> None:
    assert pt.code_path_prefix("ag-run") == "ag-"
    assert pt.code_path_prefix("p-an-stream-helper-cut") == "p-an-"


def test_every_target_has_a_short_standalone_repro_and_meta() -> None:
    assert set(up.REPROS) == set(tg.TARGETS) == set(up.META)
    for key, script in up.REPROS.items():
        assert line_count(script) < up.MAX_REPRO_LINES, key
        assert "trueup" not in script  # standalone: the library and the SDK only
        compile(script, "repro.py", "exec")


def test_pr_text_without_a_verified_fix_proposes_nothing(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    t = tg.TARGETS[("neatlogs", "anthropic messages stream")]
    text = up.pr_text({"details": {}}, t, {"fixed": False, "after_note": "no verified fix"}, tmp_path, None)
    assert "No PR is proposed" in text and "Not posted" in text

    p = build_parser()

+model call must produce exactly ONE openai.response span. Before the fix the
+responses_get_or_create_wrapper did not check SUPPRESS_LANGUAGE_MODEL_INSTRUMENTATION_KEY,
+so the openai instrumentation fired a second span for the same call even when the
+agents processor had set that suppression key.
+"""

+from unittest.mock import MagicMock, AsyncMock
+
+import pytest
+
+from opentelemetry.sdk.trace import TracerProvider
+from opentelemetry.sdk.trace.export.in_memory_span_exporter import InMemorySpanExporter

+

+    exporter = InMemorySpanExporter()

I built `trueup fix` and `trueup upstream` and ran them on all three findings, including the optional neatlogs one. All three now have a verified fix and drafted upstream text. `uv run pytest -q` passes (298 tests). Nothing was committed, pushed or posted.

**What the commands do**
- **`trueup fix <finding-id>`** finds the code behind a finding in a shallow clone (`.trueup/clones/<lib>`). The model then drafts the smallest change plus one new test, and code applies it to the clone. A try is kept only if all of these hold:
  - the new test fails before the patch and passes after;
  - the package's own test suite shows no new failure, the new test included;
  - the finding's scenarios now match truth;
  - all 57 scenarios, run against the patched package, show no new mismatch.
- A failed try goes back to the model with the reason, at most 3 tries per run. Everything is written to `fixes/<id>/`, and each run's tries are kept in `runs/`. Both workers are traced in neatlogs as `trueup-fixer` and `trueup-verifier`.
- **`trueup upstream <finding-id>`** writes `issue.md` and `pr.md` into `upstream/<id>/`, following each repo's templates (neatlogs has none). Each includes a standalone repro of 27–30 lines that needs only the library and the SDK. The repro is run on the latest release and on the patched clone, and both outputs go into the text.

**Entire's code graph was not used.** `entire agent-help` lists no graph command, and `entire graph` says the plugin isn't installed. `agent-help` marks `entire plugin` as yours to run, so I didn't install it. The fixer fell back to ripgrep plus Python's ast, and every `locate.json` records the Entire output and this reason.

**Results**

| finding | runs (tries) | before → after | suite after the patch |
|---|---|---|---|
| OpenLLMetry: double LLM spans | 5 runs, passed on try 3 of the last | ag-run 4 spans → 2 (truth 2); repro 2 spans / 14 tokens → 1 / 7 | 409 passed; the 1 failure was already there before the patch |
| OpenInference: root span OK on a failed run | 4 runs, passed on try 3 of the last | 5 scenarios OK → ERROR | 298 passed |
| neatlogs: failed `messages.stream()` shows OK | 2 runs, passed on try 1 | OK, no exception event → ERROR with one | 530 passed, same 1 error as before (a module that needs `google.genai`) |

Patching left no new mismatch in the full scenario library. Leads dropped 32 → 27 for OpenLLMetry, 19 → 14 for OpenInference and 35 → 31 for neatlogs.

**Model cost:** the key's spend went from $0.25 to $5.99 ($5.73) over 11 fix runs. The per-run figures add up to $5.42; the proxy's spend figure lags, as it did for the planner.

**Things that went wrong, all recorded in `hackathon.md`:**
- I found three holes in my own verifier during the runs. The clone wasn't reset between tries, new tests were left out of the suite comparison, and a suite that didn't run at all counted as "same failures". Because of them I withdrew two passes (one OpenLLMetry, one neatlogs) and reran those findings under the fixed rules.
- A note I wrote for the model said the Agents SDK always puts the error on the agent span. The recorded spans show it doesn't, and that cost OpenInference tries until I corrected it.
- Some new test functions also pass without the patch (3 of 4 for OpenLLMetry). Most are guards that a successful run stays OK, but the two OpenLLMetry wrapper tests would pass either way. The verifier now names such tests in every log, and each fix rests on the tests that do fail before, plus the scenarios and the repro.
- Known limits of the patches: OpenInference marks the run ERROR on any non-tool span error, even one the SDK later recovers from. neatlogs records no partial text or tokens when a stream fails.
- OpenLLMetry's own Agents SDK test suite tries to upload traces with its fake key and gets a 401. No real key is in that environment, and no key value appears in any written file.

# entire-graph — instructions for coding agents (follow directly)

You have a deterministic local code graph: `entire graph` (functions, classes, methods,
types, routes + call/inheritance relations; no network). These instructions are FOR YOU, the
agent reading this file. Use the graph to narrow exploration without trading away correctness.

## The workflow (mandatory for locate/fix/change tasks)

Your FIRST action on any task that requires finding code must be ONE search:

    entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "<the task or bug in one sentence>"

Then open the top hit's file with your file-read tool (pass a line range around the reported
line), inspect enough surrounding behavior to justify the change, and make the smallest complete
edit. Treat graph output as evidence, not an oracle.

## Hard rules

1. SEARCH FIRST — never grep/find/cat to locate code before you have searched.
2. READ focused source around the result. Widen the check when aliases, generated code, dynamic
   dispatch, or related implementations could matter.
3. Use graph follow-ups only when they answer a real question. For impact or callers, prefer:
       entire graph impact --repo . --symbol X
4. Make the smallest complete edit and check sibling sites or contracts when the task implies them.
5. VERIFY before stopping. Run the most focused relevant test, build, or reproduction available.
   If execution is unavailable, perform a bounded source-level verification and state the limit.
6. Prefer precise queries and line ranges, but never trade resolution for fewer turns.
7. Feature-detect before relying on semantic relations:
       entire graph capabilities --json

## When NOT to use the graph

If the task already names the exact file and it is small, just read it — the graph saves tokens
by eliminating exploration; when there is nothing to explore, skip it.

## Reference

    locate  ->  entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "..."
    impact  ->  entire graph impact --repo . --symbol X   (one shot: callers, callees, type consumers, data flow, co-change, siblings)
    callers ->  entire graph neighbors --repo . --symbol X --relation CALLS --direction in
    change  ->  entire graph diff --base A --head B --json
    detect  ->  entire graph capabilities --json   (inventory-only languages have no relations)
    stats   ->  entire graph stats --repo .        (human-facing token-savings report; not part of your workflow — do not run it unless asked)
=====
capabilities requires --json

If the task already names the exact file and it is small, just read it — the graph saves tokens
by eliminating exploration; when there is nothing to explore, skip it.

## Reference

    locate  ->  entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "..."
    impact  ->  entire graph impact --repo . --symbol X   (one shot: callers, callees, type consumers, data flow, co-change, siblings)
    callers ->  entire graph neighbors --repo . --symbol X --relation CALLS --direction in
    change  ->  entire graph diff --base A --head B --json
    detect  ->  entire graph capabilities --json   (inventory-only languages have no relations)
    stats   ->  entire graph stats --repo .        (human-facing token-savings report; not part of your workflow — do not run it unless asked)

Find the code for a task from a plain-language query (start here)

Usage:
  entire graph search --query "issue or concept" --repo . [--top-k 10] [--format text|json|ndjson|agent] [--head] [--profile fast|full] [--deep]

Ranked source regions for a plain-language description, with source and file:line inline, budgeted to drop straight into context. This is the first move for almost every locate task.

By default search returns: ranked candidate fix sites (top hits as full function bodies), RELATED SITES, the COVERING TEST plus other tests over the same code (ALSO COVERING), SAME-CONCEPT LITERAL (every place the concept is named, tagged EDIT/CONSUMER/DOC), a VERIFY line (the narrowest test command for the file), and a CLOSED-SET WARNING when a switch over a sealed set would fail at runtime. The three reference blocks (container map, signature types, declaration card) are OFF by default because they cost turns in agent sessions; --reference-blocks all turns them on for interactive reading.

--top-k only changes how many results come back; --deep additionally runs the exhaustive sparse (BM25) pass and fuses it with the semantic ranking (slower, reads every eligible file).

Ranking returns one region per unit, which is right for code and wrong for whole prose documents: one markdown document can hold the answer across several distant regions. So for prose the unit is the SECTION, not the file — a document's headed sections are ranked against every other section on their own scores, exactly as independent files would be (--document-resolution ranks a document as one unit instead). Separately, and on prose of any shape including headed documents, when fewer distinct units match than --top-k asked for, the spare slots are spent returning finer regions of the same document as results of their own (multi-resolution retrieval) — strictly additive, so it never displaces a unit and never breaches --max-context-bytes. --single-resolution turns that off. The two stack: a headed document can be ranked by section AND have spare slots filled with promoted passages, so a prose payload may carry both.

Flags:
  --query <text>            The task or bug in one plain sentence (required)
  --repo <path>             Repository to search (default: current repo)
  --top-k <n>               Number of results to return (default: 10)
  --format text|json|ndjson|agent
                            Output format; text is tiered for reading, agent is compact (default: json)
  --head                    Search the committed tree (cached) instead of the working tree
  --profile syntax-only|fast|full
                            Parsing depth; use full for bug-fix/locate (call-graph active) (default: fast)
  --deep                    Also run the exhaustive BM25 pass and fuse it (slower)
  --single-resolution       One result per ranked unit; do not spend spare slots on finer regions of a prose document
  --document-resolution     Rank a prose document as one unit; do not rank its sections separately
  --max-context-bytes <n>   Output byte budget; 0 = unbounded (default: 24576)
  --reference-blocks all|container-map,signature-types,type-card
                            Turn reference blocks back on (off by default)
  --max-indexed-files <n>   Bound cold-search parsing to N files
  --index-all-files         Widen cold-search parsing to every file
  --cache-dir <path>        Override the committed-tree cache directory
  --no-cache                Disable the committed-tree cache

Examples:
  entire graph search --repo . --query "token refresh returns 401" --format text --top-k 8
  entire graph search --repo . --query "csv export ordering" --profile full
Flags:
  --symbol NAME|<file>:<line>
                             Symbol to inspect (required)
  --repo <path>              Repository (default: current repo)
  --file <path>              Disambiguate an ambiguous name by file
  --line <n>                 Disambiguate by line
  --kind <kind>              Disambiguate by symbol kind
  --relation <CALLS>         Relation family to follow (default: CALLS)
  --direction both|in|out    in = callers, out = callees (default: both)
  --depth 1|2                Hops to traverse (default: 1)
  --limit <n>                Max neighbors per direction (default: 20)
  --format json|text|agent   Output format
  --max-context-bytes <n>    Output byte budget for agent format (default: 16384)
  --internal-only            Drop unresolved external endpoints
  --exclude-tests            Drop test-only neighbors
  --head                     Query the committed tree (cached)
  --profile syntax-only|fast|full
                             Parsing depth (default: full)

Examples:
  entire graph neighbors --repo . --symbol validateToken --relation CALLS --direction in
  entire graph neighbors --repo . --symbol validateToken --direction out --depth 2

Find the code for a task from a plain-language query (start here)

Usage:
  entire graph search --query "issue or concept" --repo . [--top-k 10] [--format text|json|ndjson|agent] [--head] [--profile fast|full] [--deep]

Ranked source regions for a plain-language description, with source and file:line inline, budgeted to drop straight into context. This is the first move for almost every locate task.

By default search returns: ranked candidate fix sites (top hits as full function bodies), RELATED SITES, the COVERING TEST plus other tests over the same code (ALSO COVERING), SAME-CONCEPT LITERAL (every place the concept is named, tagged EDIT/CONSUMER/DOC), a VERIFY line (the narrowest test command for the file), and a CLOSED-SET WARNING when a switch over a sealed set would fail at runtime. The three reference blocks (container map, signature types, declaration card) are OFF by default because they cost turns in agent sessions; --reference-blocks all turns them on for interactive reading.

--top-k only changes how many results come back; --deep additionally runs the exhaustive sparse (BM25) pass and fuses it with the semantic ranking (slower, reads every eligible file).

Ranking returns one region per unit, which is right for code and wrong for whole prose documents: one markdown document can hold the answer across several distant regions. So for prose the unit is the SECTION, not the file — a document's headed sections are ranked against every other section on their own scores, exactly as independent files would be (--document-resolution ranks a document as one unit instead). Separately, and on prose of any shape including headed documents, when fewer distinct units match than --top-k asked for, the spare slots are spent returning finer regions of the same document as results of their own (multi-resolution retrieval) — strictly additive, so it never displaces a unit and never breaches --max-context-bytes. --single-resolution turns that off. The two stack: a headed document can be ranked by section AND have spare slots filled with promoted passages, so a prose payload may carry both.

Flags:
  --query <text>            The task or bug in one plain sentence (required)
  --repo <path>             Repository to search (default: current repo)
  --top-k <n>               Number of results to return (default: 10)
  --format text|json|ndjson|agent
                            Output format; text is tiered for reading, agent is compact (default: json)
  --head                    Search the committed tree (cached) instead of the working tree
  --profile syntax-only|fast|full
                            Parsing depth; use full for bug-fix/locate (call-graph active) (default: fast)
  --deep                    Also run the exhaustive BM25 pass and fuse it (slower)
  --single-resolution       One result per ranked unit; do not spend spare slots on finer regions of a prose document
  --document-resolution     Rank a prose document as one unit; do not rank its sections separately
  --max-context-bytes <n>   Output byte budget; 0 = unbounded (default: 24576)
  --reference-blocks all|container-map,signature-types,type-card
                            Turn reference blocks back on (off by default)
  --max-indexed-files <n>   Bound cold-search parsing to N files
  --index-all-files         Widen cold-search parsing to every file
  --cache-dir <path>        Override the committed-tree cache directory
  --no-cache                Disable the committed-tree cache

Examples:
  entire graph search --repo . --query "token refresh returns 401" --format text --top-k 8
  entire graph search --repo . --query "csv export ordering" --profile full

"""Locate the wrapper behind a finding, and its callers, in a shallow clone of the library.

First choice is Entire's code graph. `entire agent-help` (CLI 0.11.4) lists no graph
command; `entire graph` answers that the entire-graph plugin is not installed, and
`agent-help` marks `entire plugin` as the user's to run, so Trueup does not install
it. Each run probes again and records what the CLI said. When the graph is not
there, the fallback is ripgrep for the seed symbols plus Python's ast for the
enclosing definitions, and locate.json says the graph was not used and why.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import ast
import json
import shutil
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Callable

from trueup.fixer.targets import REPOS, Target

# Installing a clone (pip/uv build) leaves copies of the source here; they are not the library's code.
BUILD_DIRS = ("build", "dist", ".eggs")

Runner = Callable[[list[str], Path | None, float], subprocess.CompletedProcess]


def run_cmd(cmd: list[str], cwd: Path | None = None, timeout: float = 600) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:
    return subprocess.run(cmd, cwd=cwd, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout)


def clone_dir(root: Path, library: str) -> Path:
    return root.resolve() / ".trueup" / "clones" / library


def ensure_clone(root: Path, library: str, run: Runner = run_cmd) -> tuple[Path, str]:
    """Shallow clone of the library's default branch. Returns (path, commit)."""
    d = clone_dir(root, library)
    if not (d / ".git").exists():
        d.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        p = run(["git", "clone", "--quiet", "--depth", "1", REPOS[library], str(d)], None, 1200)
        if p.returncode != 0:
            raise RuntimeError(f"git clone {REPOS[library]} failed: {p.stderr.strip()[-300:]}")
    p = run(["git", "-C", str(d), "rev-parse", "HEAD"], None, 60)
    return d, p.stdout.strip()


def reset_clone(clone: Path, run: Runner = run_cmd) -> None:
    """Drop every local change in the clone (only the clone)."""
    run(["git", "-C", str(clone), "reset", "--quiet"], None, 120)  # intent-to-add entries from patch.diff
    run(["git", "-C", str(clone), "checkout", "--quiet", "--", "."], None, 120)
    run(["git", "-C", str(clone), "clean", "--quiet", "-fd"], None, 120)


def probe_graph(clone: Path, seeds: tuple[str, ...], run: Runner = run_cmd) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Ask the installed Entire CLI for its code graph. Records every command and its output."""
    record: dict[str, Any] = {"used": False, "commands": []}
    if shutil.which("entire") is None:
        record["reason"] = "entire CLI not on PATH"
        return record
    for cmd in (["entire", "agent-help"], ["entire", "agent-help", "labs"], ["entire", "graph", "--help"]):
        try:
            p = run(cmd, clone, 60)
            text = (p.stdout + p.stderr).strip()
            record["commands"].append({"cmd": " ".join(cmd), "exit": p.returncode, "output": text[-3000:]})
        except (OSError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired) as e:
            record["commands"].append({"cmd": " ".join(cmd), "error": type(e).__name__})
    graph = record["commands"][-1]
    out = graph.get("output", "")
    if graph.get("exit") == 0 and "not installed" not in out:
        # The graph answered. Its subcommands are not known to this build, so keep the help
        # and let a person read it; Trueup still uses the fallback for its own results.
        record["reason"] = "entire graph answered, but Trueup has no parser for its output yet; fallback used"
    else:
        record["reason"] = ("entire graph is not available here: " + (out.splitlines()[0] if out else "no output") +
                            ". agent-help lists `entire plugin` as the user's command, so Trueup did not "
                            "install it.")
    return record

s=s[:a]+'''"""Locate the wrapper behind a finding, and its callers, in a shallow clone of the library.

First choice is Entire's code graph (the entire-graph plugin), as its agent guide says:
`entire graph capabilities --json` must list Python as a semantic language; then, per
target package, one `entire graph search --profile full` with the finding in one sentence,
and for the top hits `entire graph neighbors --relation CALLS --direction in` (callers) and
`entire graph impact`. The library's own reference pattern comes from a second search.
Every command and its JSON output is kept, with paths relative to the clone.

When the graph is not installed, does not cover Python, fails or finds nothing, the
fallback is ripgrep for the target's seed symbols plus Python's ast for the enclosing
definitions, and locate.json says the graph was not used and why.
"""'''+s[b:]
a=s.index('def probe_graph('); b=s.index('def _defs(')
s=s[:a]+'''GRAPH_TOP = 3  # search hits followed up with neighbors and impact
GRAPH_TIMEOUT = 600


def scrub(text: str, *roots: Path) -> str:
    """Remove this machine's absolute paths: each root (longest first) becomes relative, home becomes ~."""
    for r in sorted({str(x.resolve()) for x in roots}, key=len, reverse=True):
        text = text.replace(r + "/", "").replace(r, ".")
    home = str(Path.home())
    return text.replace(home + "/", "~/") if home not in ("/", "") else text


def _graph(cmd: list[str], clone: Path, run: Runner, record: dict[str, Any]) -> Any:
    """Run one `entire graph` command in the clone; record it; parsed JSON or None."""
    entry: dict[str, Any] = {"cmd": " ".join(cmd)}
    record["commands"].append(entry)
    try:
        p = run(cmd, clone, GRAPH_TIMEOUT)
    except (OSError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired) as e:
        entry["error"] = type(e).__name__
        return None
    entry["exit"] = p.returncode
    if p.returncode != 0:
        entry["error"] = (p.stderr or p.stdout).strip()[-500:]
        return None
    try:
        data = json.loads(p.stdout)
    except json.JSONDecodeError:
        entry["error"] = "output is not JSON: " + p.stdout.strip()[:200]
        return None
    entry["output"] = data
    return data


def probe_graph(clone: Path, run: Runner = run_cmd) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Is the code graph usable here for Python? Records the check."""
    record: dict[str, Any] = {"used": False, "commands": []}
    if shutil.which("entire") is None:
        record["reason"] = "entire CLI not on PATH"
        return record
    caps = _graph(["entire", "graph", "capabilities", "--json"], clone, run, record)
    if caps is None:
        err = record["commands"][-1].get("error", "")
        record["reason"] = f"entire graph is not available here: {err.splitlines()[0] if err else 'no output'}"
        return record
    # Keep what matters for Python, not the whole language table.
    record["commands"][-1]["output"] = {
        "schema_version": caps.get("schema_version"),
        "python_semantic": "Python" in caps.get("semantic_languages", []),
        "python_relations": caps.get("relation_support_by_language", {}).get("Python", []),
        "network": caps.get("features_requiring_network_access")}
    if "Python" not in caps.get("semantic_languages", []):
        record["reason"] = "entire graph has no semantic support for Python here"
        return record
    record["available"] = True
    return record


def finding_query(finding: dict[str, Any] | None, target: Target) -> str:
    """The finding in one plain sentence, as the graph's agent guide asks."""
    if not finding:
        return f"{target.code_path} wrapper records the wrong span data"
    d = finding["details"]
    ex = d.get("example") or (d.get("leads") or [{}])[0]
    return (f"{target.code_path} tracing: {d['field']} is {ex.get('trace')} in the span but really "
            f"{ex.get('truth')} ({finding['title']})")


def locate_graph(clone: Path, target: Target, query: str, record: dict[str, Any],
                 run: Runner = run_cmd) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Definitions (ranked search hits), callers and reference uses from the graph, relative to the clone."""

- **Paths:** the graph's output includes absolute paths. Everything Trueup writes under `fixes/` and `upstream/` now goes through one function that makes them relative (clone paths relative to the clone, home as `~`). The files already committed had no absolute paths to remove.
